instructors.bio: Starter lessons written by the Mahorat content team. Every lesson goes through editorial review, and courses are expanded progressively as new material is produced and approved by subject-matter experts.

courses.title: AI Fundamentals & Prompting
courses.subtitle: What modern AI really is — and how to get great results from it
courses.description: Artificial intelligence is changing how people learn and work. This course explains, in plain language, what AI systems actually do, where they fail, and how to write prompts that produce useful, reliable results.
learning_outcomes: Explain the difference between AI, machine learning and large language models
Recognise hallucinations and know how to verify AI output
Write structured prompts with context, task, constraints and format

uz.title: Sunʼiy intellekt asoslari va promptlar
uz.subtitle: Zamonaviy sunʼiy intellekt aslida nima — va undan qanday qilib yaxshi natija olish mumkin
uz.description: Sunʼiy intellekt odamlarning oʻqish va ishlash usullarini oʻzgartirmoqda. Bu kurs sunʼiy intellekt tizimlari aslida nima qilishini, ular qayerda xato qilishini va foydali, ishonchli natija beradigan promptlarni qanday yozishni oddiy tilda tushuntiradi.
learning_outcomes: Sunʼiy intellekt, mashinali oʻqitish va katta til modellari oʻrtasidagi farqni tushuntira olasiz
Gallyutsinatsiyalarni taniysiz va sunʼiy intellekt javoblarini qanday tekshirishni bilasiz
Kontekst, vazifa, cheklovlar va formatdan iborat tuzilmali promptlar yoza olasiz

courses.title: Blender: Your First Steps in 3D
courses.subtitle: From “what is 3D?” to confidently moving around your first scene
courses.description:
Blender is a free, open-source application used for 3D modeling, animation, visual effects and rendering — by hobbyists and professional studios alike.

This course begins before Blender: you will first understand **what 3D actually is**. Then you will install Blender, learn its interface and move, rotate and scale objects with the same shortcuts professionals use.
learning_outcomes: Explain vertices, edges, faces and the X/Y/Z axes
Install Blender and identify the main areas of the interface
Navigate the 3D viewport with mouse, keyboard and gizmo
Add, move, rotate and scale objects precisely
prerequisites: A computer with a dedicated or recent integrated graphics chip

uz.title: Blender: 3D olamidagi ilk qadamlar
uz.subtitle: “3D nima?” degan savoldan birinchi sahnangizda bemalol harakatlanishgacha
uz.description:
Blender — 3D modellashtirish, animatsiya, vizual effektlar va rendering uchun ishlatiladigan bepul, ochiq kodli dastur. Undan havaskorlar ham, professional studiyalar ham foydalanadi.

Bu kurs Blenderdan oldin boshlanadi: avval **3D aslida nima ekanini** tushunib olasiz. Keyin Blenderni oʻrnatasiz, uning interfeysini oʻrganasiz hamda obyektlarni mutaxassislar ishlatadigan tezkor tugmalar yordamida siljitish, aylantirish va masshtablashni oʻrganasiz.
prerequisites: Alohida yoki yangi avlod integratsiyalashgan grafik protsessorga ega kompyuter
learning_outcomes: Uchlar, qirralar, yoqlar hamda X/Y/Z oʻqlarini tushuntira olasiz
Blenderni oʻrnatib, interfeysning asosiy qismlarini aniqlay olasiz
3D koʻrinish maydonida sichqoncha, klaviatura va navigatsiya gizmosi yordamida harakatlanasiz
Obyektlarni aniq qoʻshasiz, siljitasiz, aylantirasiz va masshtablaysiz

courses.title: Computer Fundamentals from Zero
courses.subtitle: Understand the machine in front of you — no prior knowledge needed
courses.description:
This course assumes **nothing**. If you have ever wondered what actually happens inside a computer, why files have strange endings like `.pdf`, or what people mean by “hardware” and “software”, you are in the right place.

You will build a clear mental model of how a computer takes in information, works on it, stores it and shows you the result. Every term is explained the first time it appears.
learning_outcomes: Explain what a computer is using the input → processing → storage → output model
Tell hardware and software apart and name the main parts of a computer
Understand bits and bytes and read storage sizes like GB and TB
Navigate files, folders and paths with confidence
prerequisites: No prior knowledge — just curiosity and access to any computer

uz.title: Kompyuter asoslari: noldan boshlab
uz.subtitle: Oldingizdagi mashinani tushunib oling — oldindan bilim shart emas
uz.description:
Bu kurs sizdan **hech narsa** bilishni talab qilmaydi. Agar kompyuter ichida aslida nima sodir boʻlishi, fayllar nega `.pdf` kabi gʻalati qoʻshimchalar bilan tugashi yoki odamlar “apparat taʼminoti” va “dasturiy taʼminot” deganda nimani nazarda tutishi haqida oʻylab koʻrgan boʻlsangiz, toʻgʻri joydasiz.

Kompyuter maʼlumotni qanday qabul qilishi, uni qayta ishlashi, saqlashi va natijani sizga qanday koʻrsatishi haqida aniq tasavvur hosil qilasiz. Har bir atama birinchi marta uchraganda tushuntiriladi.
prerequisites: Oldindan bilim shart emas — qiziqish va istalgan kompyuterdan foydalanish imkoniyati kifoya
learning_outcomes: Kompyuter nima ekanini kiritish → qayta ishlash → saqlash → chiqarish modeli orqali tushuntira olasiz
Apparat va dasturiy taʼminotni farqlaysiz hamda kompyuterning asosiy qismlarini ayta olasiz
Bit va baytlarni tushunasiz, GB va TB kabi xotira hajmlarini oʻqiy olasiz
Fayllar, papkalar va fayl yoʻllarida bemalol harakatlanasiz

courses.title: Design Principles from Zero
courses.subtitle: Why some designs feel effortless — and how to make yours feel that way
courses.description: Good design is not decoration; it is communication. This course teaches the principles behind clear, beautiful work — hierarchy, contrast, alignment, proximity, repetition and white space — so you can judge and improve any poster, slide, website or app.
learning_outcomes: Create a clear visual hierarchy
Use contrast, alignment and proximity deliberately
Critique a layout using precise vocabulary

uz.title: Dizayn tamoyillari: noldan boshlab
uz.subtitle: Nega baʼzi dizaynlar yengil va tabiiy tuyuladi — va oʻzingiznikini qanday shunday qilish mumkin
uz.description: Yaxshi dizayn — bezak emas, balki muloqot. Bu kurs aniq va chiroyli ishlar ortidagi tamoyillarni — ierarxiya, kontrast, tekislash, yaqinlik, takrorlash va boʻsh joyni oʻrgatadi. Shunda istalgan afisha, slayd, veb-sayt yoki ilovani baholay va yaxshilay olasiz.
learning_outcomes: Aniq vizual ierarxiya yarata olasiz
Kontrast, tekislash va yaqinlikdan ongli ravishda foydalanasiz
Maketni aniq atamalar yordamida tanqidiy tahlil qila olasiz

courses.title: HTML from Absolute Zero
courses.subtitle: Build your first real web page — and understand every line of it
courses.description:
HTML is the language every web page is written in. In this course you start with **how the web works**, then write a complete page by hand.

No installs are needed beyond a text editor and a browser you already have. Each lesson explains the *why* before the *how*, so you understand the code instead of copying it.
learning_outcomes: Explain what happens between typing an address and seeing a page
Write a valid HTML document from memory
Structure content with headings, paragraphs and lists
Publish-ready habits: indentation, semantic tags and comments
prerequisites: Basic computer use: creating a file and opening it

uz.title: HTML: mutlaq noldan
uz.subtitle: Birinchi haqiqiy veb-sahifangizni yarating — va undagi har bir qatorni tushuning
uz.description:
HTML — har bir veb-sahifa yoziladigan til. Bu kursda avval **internet qanday ishlashini** bilib olasiz, soʻngra toʻliq sahifani oʻz qoʻlingiz bilan yozasiz.

Sizda allaqachon bor boʻlgan matn muharriri va brauzerdan boshqa hech narsa oʻrnatish shart emas. Har bir dars avval *nima uchun*ni, keyin *qanday qilib*ni tushuntiradi — shu tufayli kodni koʻchirib olmaysiz, balki tushunasiz.
prerequisites: Kompyuterdan oddiy foydalana olish: fayl yaratish va uni ochish
learning_outcomes: Manzilni yozganingizdan sahifani koʻrguningizgacha nima sodir boʻlishini tushuntira olasiz
Toʻgʻri HTML hujjatni yoddan yoza olasiz
Kontentni sarlavhalar, xatboshilar va roʻyxatlar yordamida tuzilmaga solasiz
Kodni nashrga tayyor yozish odatlari: chekinishlar, semantik teglar va izohlar

courses.title: Python for Complete Beginners
courses.subtitle: Your first programming language, explained without jargon
courses.description:
Python is one of the most popular programming languages in the world — used for automation, data science, AI, websites and teaching. It reads almost like English, which makes it an excellent first language.

This course starts with **what programming is** before you write a single line, then moves step by step through installing Python, running programs and working with values.
learning_outcomes: Explain what a program is and how a computer runs it
Install Python and run code in the terminal and in files
Store and change information with variables
Recognise the basic data types: text, whole numbers, decimals and true/false
prerequisites: Computer Fundamentals from Zero, or equivalent confidence with files and folders

uz.title: Python: mutlaq boshlovchilar uchun
uz.subtitle: Birinchi dasturlash tilingiz — murakkab atamalarsiz tushuntirilgan
uz.description:
Python dunyodagi eng mashhur dasturlash tillaridan biri: u avtomatlashtirish, maʼlumotlar fani, sunʼiy intellekt, veb-saytlar va taʼlimda qoʻllaniladi. Uning kodi deyarli oddiy ingliz tilidek oʻqiladi, shuning uchun u birinchi til sifatida juda qulay.

Kurs bitta ham qator yozishdan oldin **dasturlash nima ekanini** tushuntirishdan boshlanadi, keyin bosqichma-bosqich Pythonni oʻrnatish, dasturlarni ishga tushirish va qiymatlar bilan ishlashga oʻtadi.
prerequisites: “Kompyuter asoslari: noldan boshlab” kursi yoki fayl va papkalar bilan bemalol ishlay olish
learning_outcomes: Dastur nima ekanini va kompyuter uni qanday bajarishini tushuntira olasiz
Pythonni oʻrnatib, kodni terminalda va fayllarda ishga tushira olasiz
Oʻzgaruvchilar yordamida maʼlumotni saqlaysiz va oʻzgartirasiz
Asosiy maʼlumot turlarini taniysiz: matn, butun sonlar, kasr sonlar va rost/yolgʻon

courses.title: Unreal Engine Fundamentals
courses.subtitle: Understand game engines and find your way around Unreal Editor
courses.description: Unreal Engine is a professional real-time 3D engine used for games, films, architecture and simulation. This course explains what a game engine is, how to install Unreal Engine safely, and how the editor is organised — the foundation for every later Unreal course.
learning_outcomes: Explain what a game engine provides
Install Unreal Engine through the Epic Games Launcher
Navigate the editor: Viewport, Outliner, Details and Content Drawer

uz.title: Unreal Engine asoslari
uz.subtitle: Oʻyin dvigatellarini tushuning va Unreal Editor’da yoʻlingizni toping
uz.description: Unreal Engine — oʻyinlar, filmlar, arxitektura va simulyatsiyalar uchun ishlatiladigan professional real vaqt 3D dvigateli. Bu kurs oʻyin dvigateli nima ekanini, Unreal Engine’ni qanday xavfsiz oʻrnatishni va muharrir qanday tuzilganini tushuntiradi — bu keyingi barcha Unreal kurslari uchun poydevor.
learning_outcomes: Oʻyin dvigateli nimalarni taqdim etishini tushuntira olasiz
Unreal Engine’ni Epic Games Launcher orqali oʻrnata olasiz
Muharrirda harakatlanasiz: Viewport, Outliner, Details va Content Drawer

courses.title: Video Editing Fundamentals
courses.subtitle: The universal language of editing — in any app
courses.description: Before learning any particular editor, learn **editing itself**. The concepts in this course — clips, timelines, cuts, frame rates and workflow — apply equally to Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro and CapCut.
learning_outcomes: Describe what an editor does and why cuts work
Read a timeline with video and audio tracks
Choose resolution, frame rate and aspect ratio for a project
Follow a professional editing workflow from import to export

uz.title: Video montaj asoslari
uz.subtitle: Montajning universal tili — istalgan dasturda
uz.description: Biror montaj dasturini oʻrganishdan oldin **montajning oʻzini** oʻrganing. Bu kursdagi tushunchalar — kliplar, vaqt shkalasi, kesishlar, kadrlar chastotasi va ish jarayoni — Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro va CapCut uchun birdek amal qiladi.
learning_outcomes: Montajchi nima ish qilishini va kesishlar nega ishlashini tushuntira olasiz
Video va audio treklari boʻlgan vaqt shkalasini oʻqiy olasiz
Loyiha uchun ruxsat, kadrlar chastotasi va tomonlar nisbatini tanlay olasiz
Importdan eksportgacha boʻlgan professional montaj jarayoniga amal qilasiz

## Five steps from address to page

When you type `example.com` and press Enter, this happens in well under a second:

1. **Your browser asks for the address.** Computers on the internet find each other by numbers called *IP addresses*. A system called **DNS** works like a phone book and turns `example.com` into a number.
2. **The browser sends a request.** It contacts the computer at that address — a **server** — and asks: “Please send me your home page.” This conversation follows rules called **HTTP** (or **HTTPS** when it is encrypted — look for the padlock).
3. **The server responds** with files: an **HTML** file, usually some **CSS** and **JavaScript**, plus images and fonts.
4. **The browser reads the HTML** from top to bottom and builds the structure of the page.
5. **The browser paints the page** on your screen, applying styles and running scripts.

## The three languages of the web

| Language | Job | Comparison with a house |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **HTML** | Structure and content | Walls, rooms and furniture |
| **CSS** | Appearance and layout | Paint, lighting and decoration |
| **JavaScript** | Behaviour and interaction | Electricity, doors that open, the doorbell |

> [!NOTE]
> HTML is not a programming language in the strict sense — it does not make decisions or repeat steps. It is a **markup language**: it *labels* content so the browser knows what each piece is.

## Key terms

- **Browser** — the app that requests and displays web pages (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge).
- **Server** — a computer that stores a website and sends it on request.
- **URL** — the full address of a page, such as `https://example.com/about`.

uz.body_md:
## Manzildan sahifagacha besh qadam

`example.com` deb yozib Enter tugmasini bosganingizda, bir soniyaga ham yetmaydigan vaqt ichida quyidagilar sodir boʻladi:

1. **Brauzer manzilni aniqlaydi.** Internetdagi kompyuterlar bir-birini *IP-manzil* deb ataladigan raqamlar orqali topadi. **DNS** deb ataladigan tizim telefon maʼlumotnomasi kabi ishlaydi va `example.com` nomini raqamga aylantiradi.
2. **Brauzer soʻrov yuboradi.** U shu manzildagi kompyuterga — **server**ga murojaat qiladi va “Iltimos, bosh sahifangizni yuboring” deb soʻraydi. Bu muloqot **HTTP** (shifrlangan boʻlsa **HTTPS** — qulf belgisiga eʼtibor bering) deb ataladigan qoidalar asosida boradi.
3. **Server javob beradi** va fayllarni yuboradi: **HTML** fayl, odatda biroz **CSS** va **JavaScript**, shuningdek, rasmlar va shriftlar.
4. **Brauzer HTMLni** yuqoridan pastga qarab oʻqiydi va sahifa tuzilmasini quradi.
5. **Brauzer sahifani ekraningizda chizadi**: uslublarni qoʻllaydi va skriptlarni ishga tushiradi.

## Internetning uchta tili

| Til | Vazifasi | Uy bilan taqqoslash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **HTML** | Tuzilma va kontent | Devorlar, xonalar va mebel |
| **CSS** | Tashqi koʻrinish va joylashuv | Boʻyoq, yoritish va bezak |
| **JavaScript** | Xatti-harakat va interaktivlik | Elektr, ochiladigan eshiklar, qoʻngʻiroq |

> [!NOTE]
> HTML qatʼiy maʼnoda dasturlash tili emas — u qaror qabul qilmaydi va amallarni takrorlamaydi. U **belgilash tili** (*markup language*): brauzer har bir qism nima ekanini bilishi uchun kontentni *belgilab* chiqadi.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Brauzer** — veb-sahifalarni soʻrab oladigan va koʻrsatadigan ilova (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge).
- **Server** — veb-saytni saqlaydigan va soʻrov kelganda uni yuboradigan kompyuter.
- **URL** — sahifaning toʻliq manzili, masalan, `https://example.com/about`.

## A complete 3D studio

**Blender** is a free and open-source 3D creation suite developed by the Blender Foundation and a worldwide community. “Open source” means its code is public and anyone may use it — for personal or commercial work — without paying.

Blender covers the whole pipeline in one application:

- modeling and sculpting
- materials, texturing and UV unwrapping
- lighting and rendering with two engines: **EEVEE** (fast, real-time) and **Cycles** (physically accurate)
- animation and rigging
- simulations such as smoke, fluids and cloth
- video editing and compositing

## Who uses it?

Independent artists, game developers, product designers, architects and animation studios. Skills you learn in Blender — such as topology, lighting and composition — transfer to every other 3D application.

> [!TIP]
> Blender is updated often and menus move between versions. When instructions do not match your screen, check the version number on the splash screen and the official manual at docs.blender.org.

uz.body_md:
## Toʻliq 3D studiya

**Blender** — Blender Foundation (Blender jamgʻarmasi) va butun dunyodagi hamjamiyat tomonidan ishlab chiqilayotgan bepul va ochiq kodli 3D yaratish dasturlari toʻplami. “Ochiq kodli” degani — uning kodi ochiq va undan istalgan kishi shaxsiy yoki tijoriy ishlar uchun pul toʻlamasdan foydalanishi mumkin.

Blender butun jarayonni bitta dasturda qamrab oladi:

- modellashtirish va skulpting (raqamli haykaltaroshlik)
- materiallar, teksturalash va UV yoyish
- ikkita dvigatel yordamida yoritish va rendering: **EEVEE** (tezkor, real vaqt rejimida) va **Cycles** (fizik jihatdan aniq)
- animatsiya va riglash
- tutun, suyuqlik va mato kabi simulyatsiyalar
- video montaj va kompozitsiya (*compositing*)

## Undan kimlar foydalanadi?

Mustaqil rassomlar, oʻyin ishlab chiquvchilar, mahsulot dizaynerlari, arxitektorlar va animatsiya studiyalari. Blenderda oʻrganadigan koʻnikmalaringiz — topologiya, yoritish va kompozitsiya kabilar — boshqa har qanday 3D dasturga ham koʻchadi.

> [!TIP]
> Blender tez-tez yangilanadi va menyular versiyadan versiyaga joyini oʻzgartiradi. Koʻrsatmalar ekraningizga mos kelmasa, ochilish oynasidagi versiya raqamini va docs.blender.org manzilidagi rasmiy qoʻllanmani tekshiring.

contents.body_md:
## Precise recipes

A **program** is a list of instructions. **Programming** is the skill of writing those instructions so precisely that a machine with zero common sense can follow them.

Imagine explaining to a robot how to make tea. “Make tea” is not enough. You would need: *fill the kettle with water, switch it on, wait until it boils, put a tea bag in a cup, pour the water…* — every step, in order, with nothing left out. That is how programmers think.

## Why programming languages exist

Computers only understand very simple numeric instructions. Writing those directly is slow and error-prone. **Programming languages** like Python let you write instructions in readable words, and a special program translates them for the computer.

```python
print("Hello, world!")
```

This single line tells the computer to display the text `Hello, world!`. Almost every programmer’s first program does exactly this.

## Three ideas you will use forever

1. **Sequence** — instructions run one after another, top to bottom.
2. **Decisions** — do something only *if* a condition is true.
3. **Repetition** — do something many times without writing it many times.

> [!TIP]
> Mistakes in code are called **bugs**, and fixing them is **debugging**. Every programmer — including experts — writes bugs every day. Error messages are not failures; they are clues.

uz.body_md:
## Aniq retseptlar

**Dastur** — koʻrsatmalar roʻyxati. **Dasturlash** esa shu koʻrsatmalarni sogʻlom fikrdan mutlaqo mahrum mashina ham bajara oladigan darajada aniq yozish mahoratidir.

Robotga choy damlashni tushuntirayotganingizni tasavvur qiling. “Choy damla” deyish yetarli emas. Sizga shunday koʻrsatmalar kerak boʻladi: *choynakka suv quy, uni yoq, suv qaynaguncha kut, piyolaga choy paketini sol, suvni quy…* — har bir qadam, tartib bilan, hech narsani tashlab ketmasdan. Dasturchilar aynan shunday fikrlaydi.

## Dasturlash tillari nima uchun kerak

Kompyuterlar faqat juda oddiy, raqamli koʻrsatmalarni tushunadi. Ularni bevosita yozish sekin va xatoga moyil. Python kabi **dasturlash tillari** koʻrsatmalarni oʻqilishi oson soʻzlar bilan yozish imkonini beradi, maxsus dastur esa ularni kompyuter uchun tarjima qiladi.

```python
print("Salom, dunyo!")
```

Bu birgina qator kompyuterga `Salom, dunyo!` matnini ekranga chiqarishni buyuradi. Deyarli har bir dasturchining birinchi dasturi aynan shu ishni qiladi.

## Doimo foydalanadigan uchta gʻoya

1. **Ketma-ketlik** — koʻrsatmalar birin-ketin, yuqoridan pastga bajariladi.
2. **Qarorlar** — biror ishni faqat shart rost *boʻlsa* bajarish.
3. **Takrorlash** — biror ishni koʻp marta yozmasdan, koʻp marta bajarish.

> [!TIP]
> Koddagi xatolar inglizcha **bug** (“qoʻngʻiz”), ularni topib tuzatish esa **debugging** (xatolarni tuzatish) deb ataladi. Har bir dasturchi — jumladan, tajribali mutaxassislar ham — har kuni xato qiladi. Xato haqidagi xabarlar muvaffaqiyatsizlik emas, balki yoʻl koʻrsatuvchi ishoralardir.

## Order of importance

**Visual hierarchy** is the arrangement of elements so that people notice them in order of importance. In a well-designed poster you see the title first, then the key detail (date, price), and only then the small print — without trying.

## Tools that create hierarchy

- **Size** — bigger elements are seen first.
- **Weight** — bold text stands out from regular text.
- **Colour and contrast** — a bright accent on a calm background draws attention.
- **Position** — people in left-to-right languages tend to start at the top left.
- **Space** — an element surrounded by empty space feels important.

> [!TIP]
> **The squint test:** squint at your design until it blurs. Whatever still stands out is what people will notice first. If that is not the most important thing, adjust the hierarchy.

## One focal point

If everything is bold, nothing is. Choose **one** primary element per screen or page, support it with one or two secondary elements, and keep everything else quiet.

uz.body_md:
## Muhimlik tartibi

**Vizual ierarxiya** — elementlarni odamlar ularni muhimlik tartibida payqaydigan qilib joylashtirish. Yaxshi ishlangan afishada avval sarlavhani, keyin asosiy tafsilotni (sana, narx) va faqat shundan soʻng mayda yozuvni koʻrasiz — hech qanday harakat qilmasdan.

## Ierarxiya yaratuvchi vositalar

- **Oʻlcham** — kattaroq elementlar birinchi koʻrinadi.
- **Qalinlik** — qalin matn oddiy matn fonida ajralib turadi.
- **Rang va kontrast** — vazmin fondagi yorqin urgʻu rang diqqatni tortadi.
- **Joylashuv** — chapdan oʻngga yoziladigan tillarda (masalan, oʻzbek tilida) odamlar odatda yuqori chap burchakdan boshlaydi.
- **Boʻsh joy** — atrofi boʻsh joy bilan oʻralgan element muhim tuyuladi.

> [!TIP]
> **Koʻzni qisib koʻrish sinovi:** dizayningizga u xiralashguncha koʻzingizni qisib qarang. Shunda ham ajralib turgan narsani odamlar birinchi payqaydi. Agar bu eng muhim element boʻlmasa, ierarxiyani oʻzgartiring.

## Bitta asosiy nuqta

Hamma narsa qalin boʻlsa, hech narsa ajralib turmaydi. Har bir ekran yoki sahifa uchun **bitta** asosiy elementni tanlang, uni bir-ikkita ikkinchi darajali element bilan qoʻllab-quvvatlang, qolgan hamma narsani esa vazmin qoldiring.

contents.body_md:
## Three directions

A drawing on paper is **2D**: it has width and height. The real world is **3D**: it also has depth. To describe any position in 3D space we need three numbers, one for each direction, called **axes**:

- **X** — left ↔ right
- **Y** — forward ↔ back
- **Z** — up ↔ down

> [!NOTE]
> In Blender, **Z points up**. Some other programs use Y as “up”, which matters when you move models between applications.

## What a 3D object is made of

Most 3D objects are **meshes** — surfaces built from three simple parts:

- **Vertex** (plural *vertices*) — a single point in space.
- **Edge** — a straight line between two vertices.
- **Face** — a flat surface enclosed by edges, usually with three or four sides.

A cube has 8 vertices, 12 edges and 6 faces. Even a detailed character is “just” many thousands of these.

## From model to image

Making a 3D image follows a pipeline that you will learn step by step in Mahorat courses:

1. **Modeling** — building the shape.
2. **Materials and texturing** — deciding what surfaces look like: metal, wood, skin.
3. **Lighting** — placing lights, just like on a film set.
4. **Camera** — choosing what the viewer sees.
5. **Rendering** — the computer calculates the final image from all of the above.

Add **animation** — changing things over time — and you can make films and games.

uz.body_md:
## Uchta yoʻnalish

Qogʻozdagi rasm **2D** (ikki oʻlchamli): uning eni va boʻyi bor. Haqiqiy dunyo esa **3D** (uch oʻlchamli): unda chuqurlik ham mavjud. 3D fazodagi istalgan nuqtani tasvirlash uchun har bir yoʻnalish boʻyicha bittadan — jami uchta son kerak. Bu yoʻnalishlar **oʻqlar** deb ataladi:

- **X** — chap ↔ oʻng
- **Y** — old ↔ orqa
- **Z** — yuqori ↔ past

> [!NOTE]
> Blenderda **Z oʻqi yuqoriga qaragan**. Baʼzi boshqa dasturlar “yuqori” sifatida Y oʻqini ishlatadi — bu modellarni bir dasturdan boshqasiga koʻchirganda muhim.

## 3D obyekt nimalardan tashkil topgan

Aksariyat 3D obyektlar **mesh** (*mesh* — sirt toʻri) hisoblanadi, yaʼni uchta oddiy qismdan qurilgan sirtlar:

- **Uch** (*vertex*, koʻplikda *vertices*) — fazodagi bitta nuqta.
- **Qirra** (*edge*) — ikki uchni tutashtiruvchi toʻgʻri chiziq.
- **Yoq** (*face*) — qirralar bilan chegaralangan, odatda uch yoki toʻrt tomonli tekis sirt.

Kubning 8 ta uchi, 12 ta qirrasi va 6 ta yogʻi bor. Hatto juda batafsil personaj ham “bor-yoʻgʻi” shunday elementlarning minglab nusxalaridan iborat.

## Modeldan tasvirgacha

3D tasvir yaratish quyidagi jarayon (*pipeline*) asosida boradi — uni Mahorat kurslarida bosqichma-bosqich oʻrganasiz:

1. **Modellashtirish** — shaklni qurish.
2. **Materiallar va teksturalash** — sirtlar qanday koʻrinishini belgilash: metall, yogʻoch, teri.
3. **Yoritish** — xuddi kino suratga olish maydonidagidek yorugʻlik manbalarini joylashtirish.
4. **Kamera** — tomoshabin nimani koʻrishini tanlash.
5. **Rendering** — kompyuter yuqoridagilarning barchasidan yakuniy tasvirni hisoblab chiqadi.

Bunga **animatsiya**ni — vaqt oʻtishi bilan narsalarni oʻzgartirishni — qoʻshsangiz, filmlar va oʻyinlar yaratishingiz mumkin.

contents.body_md:
## Name a piece of work

You have already used many functions: `print()`, `input()`, `len()`. In this lesson you will write your own. A **function** is a named block of code you can run whenever you need it — so you write it once and use it many times.

```python
def greet(name):
    print(f"Salom, {name}!")

greet("Aziz")
greet("Malika")
```

- `def` starts a function definition; `greet` is its name.
- `name` is a **parameter** — a variable that receives a value when the function is called.
- `"Aziz"` and `"Malika"` are **arguments** — the values passed in.

## Returning a value

`print()` only shows something. To give a result **back** to the code that called the function, use `return`:

```python
def area(width, height):
    return width * height

room = area(4, 5)
print(f"The room is {room} square metres.")
```

`return` ends the function and sends the value back. Here `room` becomes `20`.

> [!WARNING]
> A function without `return` gives back the special value `None`. If you write `result = greet("Aziz")`, `result` is `None`, because `greet` prints but does not return anything.

## Default values

```python
def price_with_tax(price, tax=0.12):
    return price * (1 + tax)

print(round(price_with_tax(100000)))
print(round(price_with_tax(100000, 0.05)))
```

If no second argument is given, `tax` is `0.12`, so the first line prints `112000` and the second `105000`. (`round()` hides the tiny rounding errors that decimal numbers can have in any programming language.)

## Variables inside functions

Variables created inside a function exist only while it runs — they are **local**. This keeps functions independent: a variable called `total` inside one function does not clash with a `total` elsewhere.

## Why functions matter

- **No repetition:** fix a bug once, and every use is fixed.
- **Readability:** `average(marks)` explains itself.
- **Testing:** you can check a small function on its own.

## A worked example

```python
def average(numbers):
    """Return the average of a list of numbers."""
    return sum(numbers) / len(numbers)

def grade(mark):
    if mark >= 4.5:
        return "excellent"
    elif mark >= 3.5:
        return "good"
    return "needs practice"

marks = [5, 4, 5, 4]
avg = average(marks)
print(f"Average {avg:.1f}: {grade(avg)}")
```

The text in triple quotes is a **docstring** — a short description of what the function does. The program prints `Average 4.5: excellent`.

## Try it

Write a function `convert_to_som(dollars, rate)` that returns the amount in so'm, and a function `format_som(amount)` that returns text such as `1 250 000 so'm`. Hint: `f"{amount:,.0f}".replace(",", " ")` puts spaces between thousands.

## Common mistakes

- Printing inside a function when the result should be returned.
- Calling a function before defining it in the file.
- Forgetting the parentheses: `greet` refers to the function; `greet()` runs it.

## Key terms

- **Function** — a named, reusable block of code.
- **Parameter / argument** — the variable in the definition / the value passed in.
- **return** — sends a value back from a function.
- **Local variable** — a variable that exists only inside a function.

uz.body_md:
## Ish boʻlagiga nom berish

Siz allaqachon koʻplab funksiyalardan foydalangansiz: `print()`, `input()`, `len()`. Bu darsda oʻzingiznikini yozasiz. **Funksiya** — kerak boʻlganda istalgan vaqtda ishga tushirish mumkin boʻlgan nomli kod bloki: uni bir marta yozib, koʻp marta ishlatasiz.

```python
def greet(name):
    print(f"Salom, {name}!")

greet("Aziz")
greet("Malika")
```

- `def` funksiya taʼrifini boshlaydi; `greet` — uning nomi.
- `name` — **parametr**, yaʼni funksiya chaqirilganda qiymat oladigan oʻzgaruvchi.
- `"Aziz"` va `"Malika"` — **argumentlar**, yaʼni uzatiladigan qiymatlar.

## Qiymat qaytarish

`print()` faqat biror narsani koʻrsatadi. Natijani funksiyani chaqirgan kodga **qaytarish** uchun `return` dan foydalaning:

```python
def area(width, height):
    return width * height

room = area(4, 5)
print(f"Xona {room} kvadrat metr.")
```

`return` funksiyani tugatadi va qiymatni qaytaradi. Bu yerda `room` qiymati `20` boʻladi.

> [!WARNING]
> `return` siz funksiya maxsus `None` qiymatini qaytaradi. Agar `result = greet("Aziz")` deb yozsangiz, `result` qiymati `None` boʻladi, chunki `greet` chiqaradi, lekin hech narsa qaytarmaydi.

## Standart qiymatlar

```python
def price_with_tax(price, tax=0.12):
    return price * (1 + tax)

print(round(price_with_tax(100000)))
print(round(price_with_tax(100000, 0.05)))
```

Ikkinchi argument berilmasa, `tax` qiymati `0.12` boʻladi, shuning uchun birinchi qator `112000`, ikkinchisi `105000` ni chiqaradi. (`round()` har qanday dasturlash tilida kasr sonlarda uchraydigan juda kichik yaxlitlash xatolarini yashiradi.)

## Funksiya ichidagi oʻzgaruvchilar

Funksiya ichida yaratilgan oʻzgaruvchilar faqat u ishlab turgan paytda mavjud — ular **lokal** oʻzgaruvchilar. Bu funksiyalarni mustaqil qiladi: bir funksiya ichidagi `total` oʻzgaruvchisi boshqa joydagi `total` bilan toʻqnashmaydi.

## Funksiyalar nega muhim

- **Takrorlanish yoʻq:** xatoni bir marta tuzatsangiz, uning barcha ishlatilgan joylari tuzaladi.
- **Oʻqilishi oson:** `average(marks)` oʻzini oʻzi tushuntiradi.
- **Sinash oson:** kichik funksiyani alohida tekshirish mumkin.

## Ishlangan misol

```python
def average(numbers):
    """Sonlar roʻyxatining oʻrtacha qiymatini qaytaradi."""
    return sum(numbers) / len(numbers)

def grade(mark):
    if mark >= 4.5:
        return "aʼlo"
    elif mark >= 3.5:
        return "yaxshi"
    return "mashq kerak"

marks = [5, 4, 5, 4]
avg = average(marks)
print(f"Oʻrtacha {avg:.1f}: {grade(avg)}")
```

Uchta qoʻshtirnoq ichidagi matn — **docstring**, yaʼni funksiya nima qilishining qisqa tavsifi. Dastur `Oʻrtacha 4.5: aʼlo` ni chiqaradi.

## Oʻzingiz sinab koʻring

Summani soʻmda qaytaradigan `convert_to_som(dollars, rate)` funksiyasini va `1 250 000 so'm` kabi matn qaytaradigan `format_som(amount)` funksiyasini yozing. Maslahat: `f"{amount:,.0f}".replace(",", " ")` minglar orasiga boʻsh joy qoʻyadi.

## Keng tarqalgan xatolar

- Natijani qaytarish kerak boʻlganda uni funksiya ichida chiqarish.
- Funksiyani faylda taʼriflashdan oldin chaqirish.
- Qavslarni unutish: `greet` funksiyaning oʻziga ishora qiladi; `greet()` esa uni ishga tushiradi.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Funksiya** — nomli, qayta ishlatiladigan kod bloki.
- **Parametr / argument** — taʼrifdagi oʻzgaruvchi / uzatiladigan qiymat.
- **return** — funksiyadan qiymat qaytaradi.
- **Lokal oʻzgaruvchi** — faqat funksiya ichida mavjud boʻlgan oʻzgaruvchi.

## A machine that follows instructions

A **computer** is a machine that takes in information, follows a list of instructions to work with that information, and gives you a result. That’s it. Your laptop, your phone, a smartwatch, a cash register and the servers that run websites are all computers.

What makes computers special is not that they are clever — they are not. They are **extremely fast** and **perfectly obedient**. A modern computer can follow billions of simple instructions every second, exactly as written.

> [!NOTE]
> The list of instructions a computer follows is called a **program**. Writing programs is called **programming**.

## The four jobs of every computer

Every computer, no matter its size, does the same four jobs:

1. **Input** — receiving information. Typing on a keyboard, tapping a screen, speaking into a microphone or taking a photo are all input.
2. **Processing** — working on that information by following instructions. Adding numbers, applying a photo filter or checking a password are processing.
3. **Storage** — keeping information so it can be used later. Your photos, documents and installed apps are stored.
4. **Output** — showing or sending the result. Text on a screen, sound from a speaker, a printed page or a message sent to a friend are output.

## An everyday example

When you take a photo with your phone:

- the camera captures light — **input**
- the phone improves colours and sharpness — **processing**
- the photo is saved to the gallery — **storage**
- the photo appears on your screen — **output**

> [!TIP]
> Whenever a new technology feels confusing, ask: *what is the input, what processing happens, what is stored, and what is the output?* This one question explains a surprising amount of computing.

## Key terms

- **Computer** — a machine that follows instructions to process information.
- **Program** — a list of instructions for a computer.
- **Input / Output** — information going into / coming out of a computer.

## Koʻrsatmalarga amal qiladigan mashina

**Kompyuter** — maʼlumotni qabul qiladigan, shu maʼlumot bilan ishlash uchun koʻrsatmalar roʻyxatiga amal qiladigan va sizga natija beradigan mashina. Bor-yoʻgʻi shu. Noutbukingiz, telefoningiz, aqlli soat, kassa apparati va veb-saytlarni ishlatadigan serverlar — bularning barchasi kompyuter.

Kompyuterlarni maxsus qiladigan narsa ularning aqlli ekani emas — ular aqlli emas. Ular **nihoyatda tez** va **soʻzsiz itoatkor**. Zamonaviy kompyuter har soniyada milliardlab oddiy koʻrsatmalarni aynan yozilganidek bajara oladi.

> [!NOTE]
> Kompyuter amal qiladigan koʻrsatmalar roʻyxati **dastur** deb ataladi. Dastur yozish esa **dasturlash** deyiladi.

## Har bir kompyuterning toʻrt vazifasi

Hajmidan qatʼi nazar, har qanday kompyuter bir xil toʻrt vazifani bajaradi:

1. **Kiritish** — maʼlumotni qabul qilish. Klaviaturada yozish, ekranga teginish, mikrofonga gapirish yoki suratga olish — bularning hammasi kiritish.
2. **Qayta ishlash** — koʻrsatmalarga amal qilib, shu maʼlumot ustida ishlash. Sonlarni qoʻshish, fotosuratga filtr qoʻllash yoki parolni tekshirish — bular qayta ishlash.
3. **Saqlash** — maʼlumotni keyinroq foydalanish uchun saqlab qoʻyish. Fotosuratlaringiz, hujjatlaringiz va oʻrnatilgan ilovalaringiz saqlanadi.
4. **Chiqarish** — natijani koʻrsatish yoki yuborish. Ekrandagi matn, karnaydan chiqqan ovoz, chop etilgan sahifa yoki doʻstingizga yuborilgan xabar — bular chiqarish.

## Kundalik misol

Telefoningizda suratga olganingizda:

- kamera yorugʻlikni qayd etadi — **kiritish**
- telefon ranglar va tiniqlikni yaxshilaydi — **qayta ishlash**
- surat galereyaga saqlanadi — **saqlash**
- surat ekraningizda paydo boʻladi — **chiqarish**

> [!TIP]
> Biror yangi texnologiya chalkash tuyulsa, oʻzingizdan soʻrang: *nima kiritiladi, qanday qayta ishlanadi, nima saqlanadi va natijada nima chiqariladi?* Shu birgina savol hisoblash texnikasidagi juda koʻp narsani tushuntirib beradi.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Kompyuter** — koʻrsatmalarga amal qilib maʼlumotni qayta ishlaydigan mashina.
- **Dastur** — kompyuter uchun koʻrsatmalar roʻyxati.
- **Kiritish / Chiqarish** — kompyuterga kirayotgan / undan chiqayotgan maʼlumot.

## Two halves of every computer

Every computer is made of two kinds of things:

- **Hardware** — the physical parts you could touch: the screen, keyboard, chips and cables.
- **Software** — the instructions (programs) that tell the hardware what to do: the operating system, a web browser, a game.

Hardware without software is a box that does nothing. Software without hardware has nowhere to run. You need both.

## The main hardware parts

| Part | What it does | A simple comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CPU** (processor) | Follows instructions — the “thinking” part | A chef following a recipe |
| **RAM** (memory) | Holds what you are working on *right now* | The chef’s worktable |
| **Storage** (SSD or hard drive) | Keeps files and apps even when power is off | The pantry |
| **GPU** (graphics processor) | Draws images, video and 3D quickly | A specialist pastry chef |
| **Motherboard** | Connects every part so they can communicate | The kitchen itself |
| **Power supply / battery** | Provides electricity | The gas line |

> [!NOTE]
> **RAM is temporary.** When the power goes off, whatever is only in RAM disappears. That is why you *save* your work — saving copies it from RAM to storage.

## Kinds of software

- **Operating system (OS)** — the main program that manages the hardware and runs everything else. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.
- **Applications (apps)** — programs that help you do a task: a browser, a photo editor, a messenger.
- **Drivers** — small programs that let the operating system talk to a specific piece of hardware, such as a printer.

## Bits and bytes

Inside the computer, all information — text, photos, music — is stored as numbers made of only two digits, **0** and **1**. One such digit is a **bit**.

- 8 bits = 1 **byte** (enough to store one simple letter like “A”)
- about 1,000 bytes = 1 **kilobyte (KB)**
- about 1,000 KB = 1 **megabyte (MB)** — a typical photo is a few MB
- about 1,000 MB = 1 **gigabyte (GB)** — a film is a few GB
- about 1,000 GB = 1 **terabyte (TB)**

> [!TIP]
> When buying a computer, *storage* (e.g. 512 GB SSD) tells you how much you can keep, while *RAM* (e.g. 16 GB) tells you how much you can work on at the same time.

## Har bir kompyuterning ikki yarmi

Har qanday kompyuter ikki xil narsadan iborat:

- **Apparat taʼminoti** (inglizcha *hardware*) — qoʻl bilan ushlash mumkin boʻlgan jismoniy qismlar: ekran, klaviatura, mikrosxemalar va kabellar.
- **Dasturiy taʼminot** (inglizcha *software*) — apparatga nima qilishni aytadigan koʻrsatmalar, yaʼni dasturlar: operatsion tizim, veb-brauzer, oʻyin.

Dasturiy taʼminotsiz apparat hech narsa qilmaydigan qutidan boshqa narsa emas. Apparatsiz esa dasturiy taʼminot ishlaydigan joy yoʻq. Ikkalasi ham kerak.

## Asosiy apparat qismlari

| Qism | Vazifasi | Oddiy taqqoslash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CPU** (markaziy protsessor) | Koʻrsatmalarni bajaradi — “fikrlovchi” qism | Retsept boʻyicha ovqat tayyorlayotgan oshpaz |
| **RAM** (operativ xotira) | Ayni *hozir* ishlayotgan narsangizni ushlab turadi | Oshpazning ish stoli |
| **Doimiy xotira** (SSD yoki qattiq disk) | Elektr oʻchganda ham fayllar va ilovalarni saqlaydi | Oziq-ovqat omborxonasi |
| **GPU** (grafik protsessor) | Tasvir, video va 3D grafikani tez chizadi | Shirinliklarga ixtisoslashgan oshpaz |
| **Ona plata** (tizim platasi) | Barcha qismlarni bir-biri bilan bogʻlaydi | Oshxonaning oʻzi |
| **Quvvat bloki / batareya** | Elektr energiyasi bilan taʼminlaydi | Gaz quvuri |

> [!NOTE]
> **RAM vaqtinchalik xotira.** Elektr oʻchganda faqat RAMda turgan maʼlumot yoʻqoladi. Ishingizni aynan shuning uchun *saqlaysiz* — saqlash uni RAMdan doimiy xotiraga koʻchiradi.

## Dasturiy taʼminot turlari

- **Operatsion tizim (OT)** — apparatni boshqaradigan va qolgan barcha dasturlarni ishga tushiradigan asosiy dastur. Misollar: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.
- **Ilovalar** — biror vazifani bajarishga yordam beradigan dasturlar: brauzer, fotomuharrir, messenjer.
- **Drayverlar** — operatsion tizimga muayyan qurilma, masalan, printer bilan “gaplashish” imkonini beradigan kichik dasturlar.

## Bit va baytlar

Kompyuter ichida barcha maʼlumot — matn, fotosurat, musiqa — faqat ikki raqam, **0** va **1** dan tashkil topgan sonlar koʻrinishida saqlanadi. Bunday bitta raqam **bit** deyiladi.

- 8 bit = 1 **bayt** (“A” kabi bitta oddiy harfni saqlashga yetadi)
- taxminan 1 000 bayt = 1 **kilobayt (KB)**
- taxminan 1 000 KB = 1 **megabayt (MB)** — oddiy fotosurat bir necha MB boʻladi
- taxminan 1 000 MB = 1 **gigabayt (GB)** — film bir necha GB boʻladi
- taxminan 1 000 GB = 1 **terabayt (TB)**

> [!TIP]
> Kompyuter sotib olayotganda *doimiy xotira* (masalan, 512 GB SSD) qancha narsa saqlay olishingizni, *RAM* (masalan, 16 GB) esa bir vaqtning oʻzida qancha narsa bilan ishlay olishingizni bildiradi.

## What is a file?

A **file** is a single piece of stored information with a name: a document, a photo, a song, a program. Files live on storage (your SSD or hard drive, a USB stick, or the cloud).

Most file names end with a dot and a few letters, for example `report.pdf` or `holiday.jpg`. That ending is the **file extension**. It tells the computer what kind of file it is and which app should open it.

| Extension | Kind of file |
| --- | --- |
| `.pdf` | Document that looks the same everywhere |
| `.docx` | Word document |
| `.jpg`, `.png` | Image |
| `.mp4` | Video |
| `.mp3` | Audio |
| `.zip` | Several files compressed into one |

> [!WARNING]
> Renaming `photo.jpg` to `photo.mp4` does **not** turn a photo into a video. It only confuses the computer about which app to use.

## Folders

A **folder** (also called a *directory*) is a container for files and other folders. Folders inside folders create a tree:

```text
Documents
├── School
│   ├── math-homework.pdf
│   └── essay.docx
└── Work
    └── invoice-march.pdf
```

## Paths: a file’s address

A **path** is the full address of a file — every folder you pass through to reach it.

- On **Windows**: `C:\Users\Aziza\Documents\School\essay.docx`
- On **macOS** and **Linux**: `/Users/aziza/Documents/School/essay.docx`

Read it left to right like an address: drive or root → user → folder → sub-folder → file. Windows uses a backslash `\` between folders; macOS and Linux use a forward slash `/`.

> [!TIP]
> Good habits that professionals use:
> - Use clear names: `invoice-2026-03.pdf` beats `scan1 final FINAL.pdf`.
> - Put dates as `YYYY-MM-DD` so files sort in order.
> - Avoid spaces and special symbols in names for files you will use in code or on the web.
> - Keep a backup of important files in a second place.

## Fayl nima?

**Fayl** — nomga ega boʻlgan, saqlangan bitta maʼlumot birligi: hujjat, fotosurat, qoʻshiq yoki dastur. Fayllar doimiy xotirada (SSD yoki qattiq diskda, fleshkada yoki bulutda) joylashadi.

Koʻpchilik fayl nomlari nuqta va bir nechta harf bilan tugaydi, masalan, `hisobot.pdf` yoki `dam-olish.jpg`. Ana shu oxirgi qism **fayl kengaytmasi** deyiladi. U kompyuterga faylning turini va uni qaysi ilova ochishi kerakligini bildiradi.

| Kengaytma | Fayl turi |
| --- | --- |
| `.pdf` | Har qanday qurilmada bir xil koʻrinadigan hujjat |
| `.docx` | Word hujjati |
| `.jpg`, `.png` | Tasvir |
| `.mp4` | Video |
| `.mp3` | Audio |
| `.zip` | Bitta faylga siqilgan bir nechta fayl |

> [!WARNING]
> `rasm.jpg` faylini `rasm.mp4` deb qayta nomlash fotosuratni videoga **aylantirmaydi**. Bu faqat kompyuterni qaysi ilovadan foydalanish kerakligi borasida chalgʻitadi.

## Papkalar

**Papka** (yoki *katalog*, *direktoriya*) — fayllar va boshqa papkalar uchun idish. Papka ichidagi papkalar daraxtsimon tuzilmani hosil qiladi:

```text
Documents
├── Maktab
│   ├── matematika-uy-vazifasi.pdf
│   └── insho.docx
└── Ish
    └── hisob-faktura-mart.pdf
```

## Yoʻl: faylning manzili

**Yoʻl** (inglizcha *path*) — faylning toʻliq manzili, yaʼni unga yetib borish uchun oʻtadigan barcha papkalar.

- **Windows**da: `C:\Users\Aziza\Documents\Maktab\insho.docx`
- **macOS** va **Linux**da: `/Users/aziza/Documents/Maktab/insho.docx`

Uni manzil kabi chapdan oʻngga oʻqing: disk yoki ildiz → foydalanuvchi → papka → ichki papka → fayl. Windows papkalar orasida teskari qiya chiziq `\`, macOS va Linux esa toʻgʻri qiya chiziq `/` ishlatadi. `Users` va `Documents` kabi tizim papkalari koʻpincha inglizcha nom bilan qoladi.

> [!TIP]
> Mutaxassislar amal qiladigan foydali odatlar:
> - Aniq nom bering: `hisob-faktura-2026-03.pdf` nomi `skan1 yakuniy YAKUNIY.pdf` dan ancha yaxshi.
> - Fayllar tartib bilan saralanishi uchun sanani `YYYY-MM-DD` (yil-oy-kun) koʻrinishida yozing.
> - Kodda yoki internetda ishlatiladigan fayllar nomida boʻsh joy va maxsus belgilardan qoching.
> - Muhim fayllarning zaxira nusxasini boshqa joyda ham saqlang.

## Your first project

Build a single page called `index.html` that introduces you (or a fictional person). It must use what you have learned — and nothing more is expected.

### Requirements

1. A valid document skeleton with `lang`, `charset`, `viewport` and a `<title>`.
2. Exactly one `<h1>` with the person’s name.
3. At least two `<h2>` sections, for example *About me* and *Skills I am learning*.
4. At least two paragraphs.
5. One unordered list and one ordered list (e.g. *My goals for this year*, in order).
6. At least one `<strong>` and one `<em>` used for meaning.
7. Neat indentation.

### How to submit

Paste your HTML code in the text box, **or** upload your `index.html` file, **or** share a link if you have published it (for example with GitHub Pages).

> [!NOTE]
> A reviewer checks your work against the rubric and leaves feedback. You can resubmit after making changes.

## 1. Install Python

- **Windows:** download the latest *Python 3* installer from **python.org**. On the first screen of the installer, tick **“Add python.exe to PATH”**, then click *Install Now*.
- **macOS:** download the macOS installer from **python.org** and run it.
- **Linux:** Python 3 is usually already installed.

> [!WARNING]
> Only download Python from the official site, **python.org**. Unofficial download sites sometimes bundle unwanted software.

## 2. Open a terminal

A **terminal** is a window where you type commands instead of clicking.

- Windows: open the Start menu and search for **Terminal** (or *Command Prompt*).
- macOS: open **Terminal** from Applications → Utilities.

Check the installation:

```bash
python --version
```

On macOS and Linux you may need `python3 --version`. You should see something like `Python 3.13.1`.

## 3. Run code interactively

Type `python` (or `python3`) and press Enter. The prompt changes to `>>>`. Now type:

```python
>>> 2 + 3
5
>>> print("Salom, dunyo!")
Salom, dunyo!
```

Type `exit()` to leave.

## 4. Run a program from a file

Create a file called `hello.py` with this content:

```python
name = "Aziz"
print("Hello,", name)
print("Welcome to Python.")
```

In the terminal, move to the folder that contains the file with the `cd` command (*change directory*), for example `cd Documents`. Then run:

```bash
python hello.py
```

> [!TIP]
> Interactive mode is perfect for quick experiments. Files are for programs you want to keep and run again.

## A labelled box

A **variable** is a name that refers to a value — like a labelled box you can put something into.

```python
age = 17
city = "Samarkand"
```

The `=` sign does **not** mean “equals” as in maths. It means *“store the value on the right under the name on the left”*. Read it as “age **becomes** 17”.

You can change a variable later:

```python
age = 17
age = age + 1
print(age)  # 18
```

The text after `#` is a **comment** — a note for humans that Python ignores.

## The basic types

| Type | Name in Python | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | `str` (string) | `"Hello"` |
| Whole number | `int` (integer) | `42` |
| Decimal number | `float` | `3.14` |
| True / false | `bool` (boolean) | `True` |

Ask Python for a value’s type with `type()`:

```python
print(type("Hello"))  # <class 'str'>
print(type(42))       # <class 'int'>
```

## Naming rules

- Use letters, digits and underscores: `total_price`, `player2`.
- Do not start with a digit: `2player` is invalid.
- Names are case-sensitive: `Age` and `age` are different variables.
- Choose names that explain themselves: `minutes_per_day` beats `m`.

## Practice

Predict what this program prints **before** you run it:

```python
apples = 5
apples = apples * 2
price = 1.5
print(apples * price)
```

Then run it. Did you predict `15.0`? Multiplying an `int` by a `float` produces a `float`.

uz.body_md:
## Yorliqli quti

**Oʻzgaruvchi** — qiymatga ishora qiluvchi nom; uni ichiga biror narsa solish mumkin boʻlgan yorliqli qutiga oʻxshatish mumkin.

```python
age = 17
city = "Samarqand"
```

`=` belgisi matematikadagidek “teng” degan maʼnoni **bildirmaydi**. U *“oʻngdagi qiymatni chapdagi nom ostida saqla”* degani. Uni “age 17 ga **aylanadi**” deb oʻqing.

Oʻzgaruvchini keyinroq oʻzgartirish mumkin:

```python
age = 17
age = age + 1
print(age)  # 18
```

`#` belgisidan keyingi matn — **izoh**: Python eʼtibor bermaydigan, odamlar uchun yozilgan qayd.

## Asosiy turlar

| Tur | Pythondagi nomi | Misol |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matn | `str` (satr, *string*) | `"Salom"` |
| Butun son | `int` (*integer*) | `42` |
| Kasr son | `float` | `3.14` |
| Rost / yolgʻon | `bool` (mantiqiy qiymat, *boolean*) | `True` |

Qiymatning turini `type()` yordamida Pythondan soʻrash mumkin:

```python
print(type("Salom"))  # <class 'str'>
print(type(42))       # <class 'int'>
```

## Nomlash qoidalari

- Harflar, raqamlar va pastki chiziqdan foydalaning: `total_price`, `player2`.
- Nom raqam bilan boshlanmasin: `2player` — notoʻgʻri nom.
- Nomlar katta-kichik harfga sezgir: `Age` va `age` — ikki xil oʻzgaruvchi.
- Nomi oʻzini oʻzi tushuntiradigan boʻlsin: `minutes_per_day` nomi `m` dan yaxshiroq. Dasturchilar orasida oʻzgaruvchilarga lotin harflarida, odatda inglizcha nom berish qabul qilingan.

## Mashq

Quyidagi dastur nimani chiqarishini ishga tushirishdan **oldin** taxmin qiling:

```python
apples = 5
apples = apples * 2
price = 1.5
print(apples * price)
```

Keyin uni ishga tushiring. `15.0` deb taxmin qildingizmi? `int` ni `float` ga koʻpaytirsangiz, natija `float` boʻladi.
