## Your accounts are your keys

Email, messengers, banking and study accounts hold a large part of your life. In this lesson you will learn three habits that stop most account thefts: strong unique passwords, two-factor authentication and recognising phishing.

## Strong passwords

- **Length beats complexity.** A long passphrase of four or more random words, such as `river-lamp-orange-cloud`, is far harder to guess than `P@ss1`.
- **One password per account.** When one website is hacked, criminals try the same email and password everywhere else.
- **Use a password manager.** It creates and remembers strong, unique passwords, so you only need to remember one main password. Well-known managers are built into browsers and phones, and standalone apps exist too.

> [!WARNING]
> Never use personal information — your name, birthday or phone number — in a password. It is the first thing attackers try.

## Two-factor authentication (2FA)

2FA means logging in needs **two different proofs**: something you **know** (your password) and something you **have** (your phone or a security key).

- An **authenticator app** shows a new six-digit code every 30 seconds — the recommended option.
- An **SMS code** is weaker, because phone numbers can be hijacked, but it is still much better than no second factor.
- **Passkeys** let you sign in with your fingerprint or face instead of a password, and cannot be phished.

Turn on 2FA first for your email account — it can reset all your other passwords.

## Phishing

**Phishing** is a message that pretends to be from someone you trust — a bank, a delivery company, a messenger's support team — to trick you into giving away a password or code.

Warning signs:

- **Urgency or threats:** “Your card will be blocked in one hour.”
- **A link that does not match:** the text says your bank, but the address is something like `bank-secure-login.example`.
- **A request for a one-time code.** No real bank or messenger will ever ask you to tell them a code you received by SMS.

> [!TIP]
> If a message worries you, do not use its links or phone numbers. Open the official app or call the number printed on your bank card.

## If you clicked a phishing link

1. Change the password of that account immediately (and anywhere you reused it).
2. Turn on 2FA if it was off.
3. Check the account's list of active sessions or devices and sign out ones you do not recognise.
4. If money or a bank card is involved, call your bank straight away.

## Try it

Turn on two-factor authentication for your main email account using an authenticator app. Then look at a recent message from a company and check the real address behind its links.

## Common mistakes

- Reusing one password for several sites.
- Telling a one-time code to someone on the phone who “works at the bank”.
- Trusting a message because it shows a familiar logo.

## Key terms

- **Passphrase** — a long password made of several words.
- **Password manager** — an app that creates and stores unique passwords.
- **Two-factor authentication (2FA)** — logging in with two different proofs of identity.
- **Phishing** — a fake message designed to steal passwords, codes or money.

uz.body_md:
## Hisoblaringiz — sizning kalitlaringiz

Elektron pochta, messenjerlar, bank va oʻqish hisoblari hayotingizning katta qismini saqlaydi. Bu darsda hisoblar oʻgʻirlanishining aksariyatini toʻxtatadigan uchta odatni oʻrganasiz: kuchli va takrorlanmas parollar, ikki bosqichli autentifikatsiya hamda fishingni tanib olish.

## Kuchli parollar

- **Uzunlik murakkablikdan muhimroq.** `daryo-chiroq-apelsin-bulut` kabi toʻrt va undan ortiq tasodifiy soʻzdan iborat uzun parol iborasini topish `P@ss1` dan ancha qiyin.
- **Har bir hisob uchun alohida parol.** Bitta sayt buzilganda jinoyatchilar oʻsha email va parolni boshqa barcha joylarda sinab koʻradi.
- **Parollar menejeridan foydalaning.** U kuchli va takrorlanmas parollarni yaratadi va eslab qoladi, shuning uchun siz faqat bitta asosiy parolni eslab qolishingiz kifoya. Mashhur menejerlar brauzer va telefonlarga oʻrnatilgan, alohida ilovalar ham bor.

> [!WARNING]
> Parolda hech qachon shaxsiy maʼlumotlardan — ismingiz, tugʻilgan kuningiz yoki telefon raqamingizdan foydalanmang. Hujumchilar birinchi navbatda aynan shularni sinab koʻradi.

## Ikki bosqichli autentifikatsiya (2FA)

2FA — tizimga kirish uchun **ikki xil dalil** kerak degani: siz **biladigan** narsa (parolingiz) va sizda **bor** narsa (telefoningiz yoki xavfsizlik kaliti).

- **Autentifikator ilovasi** har 30 soniyada yangi olti xonali kod koʻrsatadi — tavsiya etiladigan usul.
- **SMS kod** kuchsizroq, chunki telefon raqamini egallab olish mumkin, ammo u baribir ikkinchi bosqichning umuman yoʻqligidan ancha yaxshi.
- **Passkey** (kirish kaliti) parol oʻrniga barmoq izi yoki yuz bilan kirish imkonini beradi va uni fishing orqali oʻgʻirlab boʻlmaydi.

2FA ni birinchi navbatda elektron pochtangiz uchun yoqing — u orqali boshqa barcha parollarni tiklash mumkin.

## Fishing

**Fishing** — parol yoki kodni berib qoʻyishingiz uchun siz ishonadigan kimsa — bank, yetkazib berish xizmati yoki messenjerning qoʻllab-quvvatlash xizmati nomidan yuborilgan soxta xabar.

Ogohlantiruvchi belgilar:

- **Shoshiltirish yoki tahdid:** “Kartangiz bir soatdan keyin bloklanadi.”
- **Mos kelmaydigan havola:** matnda bankingiz nomi yozilgan, lekin manzil `bank-secure-login.example` ga oʻxshash.
- **Bir martalik kodni soʻrash.** Hech bir haqiqiy bank yoki messenjer sizdan SMS orqali kelgan kodni aytishingizni soʻramaydi.

> [!TIP]
> Biror xabar sizni xavotirga solsa, undagi havola yoki telefon raqamlaridan foydalanmang. Rasmiy ilovani oching yoki bank kartangizda yozilgan raqamga qoʻngʻiroq qiling.

## Agar fishing havolasini bosib qoʻygan boʻlsangiz

1. Oʻsha hisob parolini (va u takrorlangan barcha joylarda) darhol oʻzgartiring.
2. Agar 2FA oʻchiq boʻlsa, uni yoqing.
3. Hisobdagi faol seanslar yoki qurilmalar roʻyxatini tekshiring va tanimaganlaringizdan chiqib keting.
4. Agar pul yoki bank kartasi bilan bogʻliq boʻlsa, darhol bankingizga qoʻngʻiroq qiling.

## Oʻzingiz sinab koʻring

Asosiy elektron pochta hisobingiz uchun autentifikator ilovasi orqali ikki bosqichli autentifikatsiyani yoqing. Soʻngra biror kompaniyadan kelgan soʻnggi xabarni ochib, undagi havolalarning haqiqiy manzilini tekshiring.

## Keng tarqalgan xatolar

- Bitta parolni bir nechta saytda ishlatish.
- “Bankda ishlayman” degan kishiga telefonda bir martalik kodni aytib berish.
- Xabarda tanish logotip borligi uchun unga ishonish.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Parol iborasi** (*passphrase*) — bir nechta soʻzdan iborat uzun parol.
- **Parollar menejeri** — takrorlanmas parollarni yaratadigan va saqlaydigan ilova.
- **Ikki bosqichli autentifikatsiya (2FA)** — shaxsni ikki xil dalil bilan tasdiqlab kirish.
- **Fishing** — parol, kod yoki pulni oʻgʻirlash uchun yuborilgan soxta xabar.

## Your project

A relative or friend needs a computer for study or work. Prepare a short plan, as an IT professional would, that covers choosing, setting up and protecting it.

### What to deliver

1. **Who it is for** — the person, what they will use the computer for, and the budget.
2. **Specification** — processor, RAM, storage and ports, with one sentence explaining each choice.
3. **Setup plan** — user accounts (administrator and standard), updates, and the software to install from official sources.
4. **Backup plan** — which files matter and how the 3-2-1 rule is met.
5. **Security plan** — password manager, two-factor authentication for key accounts, and three phishing warning signs you will teach them.

### How to submit

Write your plan in the text box (about one page), upload it as a document, or share a link to it.

> [!NOTE]
> A reviewer checks your plan against the rubric and leaves feedback. You can improve it and resubmit.

## The manager of the computer

You already know that the **operating system (OS)** is the main program that runs everything else. In this lesson you will see what it manages for you — and which of its settings keep you safe.

The OS has five main jobs:

1. **Hardware** — it talks to the processor, memory, storage and devices through drivers.
2. **Programs** — it starts apps, shares processor time between them and stops them.
3. **Files** — it organises storage into files and folders.
4. **Users and security** — it keeps each person's files separate and decides who may do what.
5. **Interface** — it gives you the desktop, windows, menus and touch gestures.

Common operating systems are Windows, macOS and Linux on computers, and Android and iOS on phones.

## Users and accounts

Each person who uses a computer should have their own **user account**, with their own files and settings.

- An **administrator** account can install software and change system settings.
- A **standard** account can use apps but needs an administrator's approval for system changes.

> [!TIP]
> Using a standard account for everyday work limits the damage if you open a harmful file by mistake: malware cannot change the system without asking.

## Permissions

Apps must ask before using sensitive things such as the camera, microphone, location, contacts or your files. Grant only what an app genuinely needs. A flashlight app has no reason to read your contacts.

- **Windows:** **Settings → Privacy & security**.
- **macOS:** **System Settings → Privacy & Security**.
- **Phones:** **Settings → Apps** (Android) or **Settings → Privacy & Security** (iOS).

## Updates

OS updates fix security holes that criminals actively use. Install them promptly, and restart when asked — many updates only finish after a restart.

## Seeing what is running

When an app freezes, the OS can show you what is happening:

- **Windows:** **Task Manager** (**Ctrl + Shift + Esc**) lists running apps and how much CPU and memory each uses. Select a frozen app and choose **End task**.
- **macOS:** **Activity Monitor** (in **Applications → Utilities**) does the same; **Force Quit** stops a frozen app (**Option + Command + Esc**).

## Try it

1. Find which version of your operating system you are running.
2. Open the privacy settings and check which apps may use your camera and microphone.
3. Open Task Manager or Activity Monitor and find the app using the most memory.

## Common mistakes

- Postponing updates for weeks.
- Using an administrator account for everything.
- Allowing every permission an app asks for without thinking.

## Key terms

- **Operating system (OS)** — the program that manages the hardware and runs all other programs.
- **Administrator / standard account** — an account that can or cannot change the system.
- **Permission** — an app's right to use something sensitive, such as the camera.
- **Task Manager / Activity Monitor** — tools that show running programs.

uz.body_md:
## Kompyuterning boshqaruvchisi

Siz **operatsion tizim (OT)** qolgan barcha dasturlarni ishga tushiradigan asosiy dastur ekanini allaqachon bilasiz. Bu darsda u siz uchun nimalarni boshqarishini — va uning qaysi sozlamalari sizni xavfsiz saqlashini koʻrasiz.

Operatsion tizimning beshta asosiy vazifasi bor:

1. **Apparat** — u drayverlar orqali protsessor, xotira, doimiy xotira va qurilmalar bilan aloqa qiladi.
2. **Dasturlar** — ilovalarni ishga tushiradi, protsessor vaqtini ular oʻrtasida taqsimlaydi va ularni toʻxtatadi.
3. **Fayllar** — doimiy xotirani fayl va papkalarga ajratib tartibga soladi.
4. **Foydalanuvchilar va xavfsizlik** — har bir odamning fayllarini alohida saqlaydi va kim nima qila olishini hal qiladi.
5. **Interfeys** — sizga ish stoli, oynalar, menyular va sensorli imo-ishoralarni taqdim etadi.

Keng tarqalgan operatsion tizimlar: kompyuterlarda Windows, macOS va Linux, telefonlarda Android va iOS.

## Foydalanuvchilar va hisoblar

Kompyuterdan foydalanadigan har bir kishining oʻz fayllari va sozlamalari bilan alohida **foydalanuvchi hisobi** boʻlishi kerak.

- **Administrator** hisobi dasturlarni oʻrnatishi va tizim sozlamalarini oʻzgartirishi mumkin.
- **Standart** hisob ilovalardan foydalana oladi, ammo tizimdagi oʻzgarishlar uchun administrator ruxsati kerak.

> [!TIP]
> Kundalik ish uchun standart hisobdan foydalanish zararli faylni bilmasdan ochib qoʻysangiz, zararni cheklaydi: zararli dastur soʻramasdan tizimni oʻzgartira olmaydi.

## Ruxsatlar

Ilovalar kamera, mikrofon, joylashuv, kontaktlar yoki fayllaringiz kabi maxfiy narsalardan foydalanishdan oldin ruxsat soʻrashi shart. Faqat ilovaga haqiqatan kerak boʻlgan ruxsatni bering. Fonar ilovasining kontaktlaringizni oʻqishiga hech qanday sabab yoʻq.

- **Windows:** **Settings → Privacy & security**.
- **macOS:** **System Settings → Privacy & Security**.
- **Telefonlar:** **Settings → Apps** (Android) yoki **Settings → Privacy & Security** (iOS).

## Yangilanishlar

Operatsion tizim yangilanishlari jinoyatchilar faol foydalanadigan xavfsizlik teshiklarini yopadi. Ularni kechiktirmasdan oʻrnating va soʻralganda qayta ishga tushiring — koʻplab yangilanishlar faqat qayta ishga tushirilgandan keyin yakunlanadi.

## Nima ishlayotganini koʻrish

Ilova qotib qolganda operatsion tizim nima boʻlayotganini koʻrsata oladi:

- **Windows:** **Task Manager** (**Ctrl + Shift + Esc**) ishlab turgan ilovalarni va ularning har biri qancha protsessor va xotira ishlatayotganini koʻrsatadi. Qotib qolgan ilovani tanlab, **End task** ni bosing.
- **macOS:** **Activity Monitor** (**Applications → Utilities** ichida) xuddi shu ishni qiladi; **Force Quit** qotib qolgan ilovani toʻxtatadi (**Option + Command + Esc**).

## Oʻzingiz sinab koʻring

1. Operatsion tizimingizning qaysi versiyasi oʻrnatilganini toping.
2. Maxfiylik sozlamalarini ochib, qaysi ilovalar kamera va mikrofondan foydalana olishini tekshiring.
3. Task Manager yoki Activity Monitor ni ochib, eng koʻp xotira ishlatayotgan ilovani toping.

## Keng tarqalgan xatolar

- Yangilanishlarni haftalab kechiktirish.
- Hamma ish uchun administrator hisobidan foydalanish.
- Ilova soʻragan har bir ruxsatni oʻylamasdan berish.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Operatsion tizim (OT)** — apparatni boshqaradigan va qolgan barcha dasturlarni ishga tushiradigan dastur.
- **Administrator / standart hisob** — tizimni oʻzgartira oladigan yoki oʻzgartira olmaydigan hisob.
- **Ruxsat** — ilovaning kamera kabi maxfiy narsadan foydalanish huquqi.
- **Task Manager / Activity Monitor** — ishlab turgan dasturlarni koʻrsatadigan vositalar.

## What forms are for

Forms let people send information: signing up, searching, ordering, leaving feedback. In this lesson you will build a complete registration form with labels and validation that the browser checks for you.

```html
<form action="/register" method="post">
  <label for="name">Full name</label>
  <input id="name" name="name" type="text" required>

  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>

  <label for="level">Your level</label>
  <select id="level" name="level">
    <option value="zero">Complete beginner</option>
    <option value="some">I know a little</option>
  </select>

  <label for="goal">What do you want to learn?</label>
  <textarea id="goal" name="goal" rows="4"></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Sign up</button>
</form>
```

## Labels are not optional

Every input needs a `<label>`. The label's `for` must match the input's `id`. Then:

- screen readers announce what the field is for,
- clicking the label puts the cursor in the field — a bigger target on phones.

> [!WARNING]
> A `placeholder` is not a label. It disappears as soon as someone starts typing and is often too faint to read. Use it only for an example, such as `placeholder="name@example.com"`.

## Choosing the right input type

| Type | Use it for | Bonus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | Names and short text | — |
| `email` | Email addresses | Checks the format; phones show an @ keyboard |
| `password` | Passwords | Hides the characters |
| `number` | Quantities | Number keyboard and arrows |
| `date` | Dates | A date picker |
| `checkbox` | Yes/no choices | Each can be ticked separately |
| `radio` | One choice from several | Give all options the same `name` |

## Built-in validation

The browser checks these attributes before the form is sent:

- `required` — the field cannot be empty.
- `minlength` and `maxlength` — limits on the number of characters.
- `min` and `max` — limits for numbers and dates.

Browser validation helps people fix mistakes quickly, but it can be bypassed. A real website must always check the data again on the server.

## Where the data goes

The `action` attribute is the address that receives the data, and `method` says how it is sent: `get` puts the data in the URL (good for searches), `post` sends it in the body of the request (for sign-ups and anything private). Receiving the data needs a server, which you will learn about in backend courses. For now, focus on building the form correctly.

## Try it

Build a feedback form with a name, an email, a rating from 1 to 5 (radio buttons sharing one `name`), a message and a submit button. Make the name and email required, then try submitting it empty to see the browser's messages.

## Common mistakes

- Inputs without labels, or using placeholders instead.
- Forgetting the `name` attribute, so the field's value is never sent.
- Using `type="text"` for everything and losing the right keyboard on phones.

## Key terms

- **Form** — a group of fields that sends data.
- **Label** — the visible name of a field, linked with `for` and `id`.
- **Validation** — checking that input is complete and in the right format.
- **GET / POST** — two ways of sending form data.

## Formalar nima uchun kerak

Formalar odamlarga maʼlumot yuborish imkonini beradi: roʻyxatdan oʻtish, qidirish, buyurtma berish, fikr qoldirish. Bu darsda yorliqlari va brauzer oʻzi tekshiradigan validatsiyasi bor toʻliq roʻyxatdan oʻtish formasini yaratasiz.

```html
<form action="/register" method="post">
  <label for="name">Ism-sharifingiz</label>
  <input id="name" name="name" type="text" required>

  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>

  <label for="level">Darajangiz</label>
  <select id="level" name="level">
    <option value="zero">Mutlaq boshlovchi</option>
    <option value="some">Bir oz bilaman</option>
  </select>

  <label for="goal">Nimani oʻrganmoqchisiz?</label>
  <textarea id="goal" name="goal" rows="4"></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Roʻyxatdan oʻtish</button>
</form>
```

## Yorliqlar majburiy

Har bir maydonga `<label>` (yorliq) kerak. Yorliqning `for` qiymati maydonning `id` siga mos kelishi shart. Shunda:

- ekran oʻquvchi dasturlar maydon nima uchun ekanini aytadi,
- yorliqni bosish kursorni maydonga qoʻyadi — telefonlarda bosish uchun kattaroq joy.

> [!WARNING]
> `placeholder` yorliq emas. U yozishni boshlashingiz bilanoq yoʻqoladi va koʻpincha oʻqish uchun juda xira boʻladi. Undan faqat namuna uchun foydalaning, masalan, `placeholder="name@example.com"`.

## Maydonning toʻgʻri turini tanlash

| Tur | Nima uchun | Qoʻshimcha qulaylik |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | Ismlar va qisqa matn | — |
| `email` | Email manzillar | Formatni tekshiradi; telefonda @ belgili klaviatura chiqadi |
| `password` | Parollar | Belgilarni yashiradi |
| `number` | Miqdorlar | Raqamli klaviatura va strelkalar |
| `date` | Sanalar | Sana tanlash oynasi |
| `checkbox` | Ha/yoʻq tanlovlari | Har birini alohida belgilash mumkin |
| `radio` | Bir nechtadan bittasini tanlash | Barcha variantlarga bir xil `name` bering |

## Oʻrnatilgan validatsiya

Brauzer forma yuborilishidan oldin quyidagi atributlarni tekshiradi:

- `required` — maydon boʻsh qolishi mumkin emas.
- `minlength` va `maxlength` — belgilar soniga cheklov.
- `min` va `max` — sonlar va sanalar uchun cheklov.

Brauzer validatsiyasi odamlarga xatolarni tez tuzatishga yordam beradi, ammo uni chetlab oʻtish mumkin. Haqiqiy veb-sayt maʼlumotlarni har doim serverda qayta tekshirishi kerak.

## Maʼlumotlar qayerga boradi

`action` atributi maʼlumotlarni qabul qiladigan manzil, `method` esa ular qanday yuborilishini bildiradi: `get` maʼlumotlarni URL ga qoʻshadi (qidiruv uchun qulay), `post` ularni soʻrov tanasida yuboradi (roʻyxatdan oʻtish va har qanday maxfiy maʼlumot uchun). Maʼlumotlarni qabul qilish uchun server kerak — u haqida backend kurslarida oʻrganasiz. Hozircha formani toʻgʻri yaratishga eʼtibor qarating.

## Oʻzingiz sinab koʻring

Ism, email, 1 dan 5 gacha baho (bir xil `name` ga ega radio tugmalar), xabar va yuborish tugmasidan iborat fikr-mulohaza formasini yarating. Ism va emailni majburiy qiling, soʻngra brauzer xabarlarini koʻrish uchun uni boʻsh holda yuborib koʻring.

## Keng tarqalgan xatolar

- Yorliqsiz maydonlar yoki yorliq oʻrniga placeholder ishlatish.
- `name` atributini unutish — maydon qiymati umuman yuborilmaydi.
- Hamma narsa uchun `type="text"` dan foydalanish va telefonlarda mos klaviaturani yoʻqotish.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Forma** — maʼlumot yuboradigan maydonlar guruhi.
- **Yorliq** (*label*) — maydonning `for` va `id` orqali bogʻlangan koʻrinadigan nomi.
- **Validatsiya** — kiritilgan maʼlumot toʻliq va toʻgʻri formatda ekanini tekshirish.
- **GET / POST** — forma maʼlumotlarini yuborishning ikki usuli.

## Elements that describe their role Before HTML5, pages were built from many anonymous `
` elements. Today we use **semantic elements** that say what each part of the page is. In this lesson you will structure a page with them and test it the way people with disabilities use the web. ```html
Aziza's portfolio
  • Home
  • Projects
  • Contact

Projects

Weather widget

A small page that shows the forecast for Tashkent.

© 2026 Aziza Karimova

``` | Element | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `
` | Introductory content, often the logo and navigation | | `
` | A group of main navigation links | | `
` | The main content — only one per page | | `
` | A self-contained piece, such as a post or a project | | `
` | A themed section with its own heading | | `
` | Related, secondary content | | `
` | Closing information, such as copyright or contacts | ## Why semantics matter - **Screen readers** list these **landmarks**, so users can jump straight to the navigation or the main content. - **Search engines** understand the structure of your page better. - **Developers** — including you, later — read the code more easily. ## Accessibility basics Accessibility means everyone can use your site, including people who are blind, have low vision, cannot use a mouse or have a temporary injury. Most of it comes from HTML you already know: 1. Set the page language: `` or `lang="en"`. 2. Use headings in order. 3. Give every image suitable alt text. 4. Give every form field a label. 5. Make sure everything works with the keyboard alone. 6. Keep strong contrast between text and background. 7. Write link text that makes sense on its own. ## Test it yourself - **Keyboard test:** put the mouse aside and press **Tab** to move through the page and **Enter** to follow links. You should always see where the focus is. - **Screen reader:** try VoiceOver on Mac and iPhone, TalkBack on Android or the free NVDA on Windows for a few minutes. - **Automatic check:** in Chrome, open **DevTools → Lighthouse** and run an **Accessibility** audit. > [!NOTE] > Automatic tools find only some problems. A keyboard test and a few minutes with a screen reader reveal much more. ## Try it Rewrite a page built only from `
` elements using `header`, `nav`, `main`, `article` and `footer`. Then do the keyboard test and fix anything you cannot reach. ## Common mistakes - Several `
` elements on one page. - Choosing headings by size instead of structure. - Removing the focus outline with CSS, so keyboard users get lost. ## Key terms - **Semantic element** — an element whose name describes its meaning. - **Landmark** — a region (header, nav, main, footer) that assistive technology can jump to. - **Accessibility** — designing so that everyone can use a site. - **Focus** — the element that currently receives keyboard input.

` | Asosiy navigatsiya havolalari guruhi | | `

If the information would make sense in a spreadsheet, a table is right. In this lesson you will build a correct, accessible HTML table. > [!WARNING] > Never use tables to arrange the layout of a page (for example, to put a menu beside the text). That was common in the 1990s; today layout is a job for CSS, and layout tables confuse screen readers. ## Building a table ```html

Use merging sparingly — complex tables are hard to read on small screens and for screen-reader users. ## Try it Build a table of your weekly timetable (or a fictional one) with a caption, a header row and at least five days as rows. ## The “hyper” in hypertext Links are what make the web a web. In this lesson you will create links to other sites, to your own pages and to places within a page. ```html MDN Web Docs ``` `` stands for **anchor**. The `href` attribute holds the destination; the text between the tags is what people click. ## Absolute and relative addresses - An **absolute URL** contains the full address, including `https://`. Use it for other websites. - A **relative URL** describes where a file is **compared to the current page**. Use it for pages and files in your own site. Imagine this site: ```text my-site/ ├── index.html ├── about.html └── projects/ └── game.html ``` | From | To | Relative link | | --- | --- | --- | | `index.html` | `about.html` | `about.html` | | `index.html` | `projects/game.html` | `projects/game.html` | | `projects/game.html` | `index.html` | `../index.html` | `../` means “go up one folder”. Relative links keep working when you move the whole site to a server. ## Links within a page Give an element an `id`, then link to it with `#`: ```html Jump to contact details

Contact

``` ## Opening a new tab ```html Example (opens in a new tab) ``` `target="_blank"` opens a new tab. Add `rel="noopener"` so the new page cannot control yours. Open new tabs only when there is a good reason, and say so in the link text. ## Email and phone links - `Email us` opens the email app. - `Call us` starts a call on phones. ## Writing good link text Link text should make sense on its own. Screen-reader users often jump from link to link, hearing only the link text. > [!TIP] > Write “Read the timetable” instead of “Click here”. Clear link text also helps search engines understand your pages. ## Try it Create `index.html` and `about.html` in the same folder. Add a navigation list to each page that links to the other one, and add a link that jumps to a section further down the page. ## Common mistakes - Using absolute paths from your own computer (`C:\Users\...`) — they break on any other device. - Forgetting `https://` for external links, so the browser treats them as files in your site. - Vague link text such as “here” or “more”. ## Key terms - **Anchor (``)** — the link element. - **Absolute URL** — a full address including the protocol. - **Relative URL** — an address relative to the current file. - **Fragment (`#id`)** — a link to a place within a page.

## Your final project

Build a small **portfolio site** about yourself (or a fictional person) and publish it with GitHub Pages. It brings together everything in this course.

### Requirements

1. At least three pages: **Home**, **Projects** and **Contact**, linked by the same navigation on every page.
2. A valid document skeleton on every page, with `lang`, `charset`, `viewport` and a unique `<title>`.
3. Semantic layout: `header`, `nav`, `main` and `footer`, with a correct heading outline.
4. At least three images with suitable alt text, sensible file sizes, and `width` and `height`.
5. One table (for example, skills and levels) or a well-structured list of projects.
6. A contact form with labels, suitable input types and `required` fields (it does not need to send messages yet).
7. The keyboard test passes: everything can be reached with Tab and the focus is visible.
8. Published on GitHub Pages.

### How to submit

Submit the URL of your published site. You can also add a short note about what you are most proud of and what you would improve.

> [!NOTE]
> A reviewer checks your site against the rubric and leaves feedback. You can update the site and resubmit.

## What “publishing” means

So far your pages have lived on your computer. **Publishing** means copying them to a **web server** so anyone can open them with a URL. **GitHub Pages** is a free service that publishes static sites (HTML, CSS, images) straight from a GitHub repository. In this exercise you will publish your site.

## Prepare your folder

```text
my-site/
├── index.html
├── projects.html
├── contact.html
└── images/
    └── profile.jpg
```

- The home page must be called `index.html` and sit at the top of the folder.
- Use only relative links between your pages.
- Use lowercase file names without spaces. Web servers are **case-sensitive**: `Photo.JPG` and `photo.jpg` are different files.

## Step by step

1. Create a free account at **github.com** and turn on two-factor authentication.
2. Click **New repository**. Name it `your-username.github.io` (replace with your GitHub user name), make it **Public** and create it.
3. On the repository page, choose **Add file → Upload files**, drag in the contents of your site folder (not the folder itself) and click **Commit changes**.
4. Open **Settings → Pages**. Under **Build and deployment**, check that the source is **Deploy from a branch**, the branch is **main** and the folder is **/ (root)**, then save.
5. After a minute or two, your site is live at `https://your-username.github.io/`.

## Updating your site

Upload changed files the same way, or edit them directly on GitHub. Every commit republishes the site within a minute or two. If you do not see the change, refresh the page with **Ctrl + F5** (Windows) or **Cmd + Shift + R** (Mac).

> [!WARNING]
> A published site is public. Do not put your home address, phone number, passport details or anything else private on it.

## Checking the result

- Open the site on your phone as well as your computer.
- Click every link and check that every image appears.
- Run the keyboard test from the previous lesson.

## Try it

Publish your profile page from the earlier project. Send the link to a friend and ask them whether everything works on their phone.

## Common mistakes

- `index.html` inside a sub-folder instead of at the top, so the home page shows a 404 error.
- Links that differ from file names only by capital letters.
- Links pointing to files on your computer (`C:\...`) instead of relative paths.

## Key terms

- **Web server** — a computer that sends web pages to browsers.
- **Static site** — a site made of fixed files, without server-side code.
- **Repository** — a project folder on GitHub with its history.
- **Commit** — a saved change in a repository.

## “Eʼlon qilish” nimani anglatadi

Hozirgacha sahifalaringiz kompyuteringizda edi. **Eʼlon qilish** — ularni istalgan kishi URL orqali ocha olishi uchun **veb-serverga** koʻchirish demakdir. **GitHub Pages** — statik saytlarni (HTML, CSS, rasmlar) toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri GitHub repozitoriyasidan eʼlon qiladigan bepul xizmat. Bu mashqda saytingizni eʼlon qilasiz.

## Papkangizni tayyorlang

```text
my-site/
├── index.html
├── projects.html
├── contact.html
└── images/
    └── profile.jpg
```

- Bosh sahifa `index.html` deb nomlanishi va papkaning eng yuqori qismida turishi shart.
- Sahifalaringiz orasida faqat nisbiy havolalardan foydalaning.
- Fayl nomlarini kichik harflarda va boʻsh joysiz yozing. Veb-serverlar **katta-kichik harfni farqlaydi**: `Photo.JPG` va `photo.jpg` — ikki xil fayl.

## Qadamma-qadam

1. **github.com** saytida bepul hisob yarating va ikki bosqichli autentifikatsiyani yoqing.
2. **New repository** tugmasini bosing. Uni `your-username.github.io` deb nomlang (oʻrniga GitHub foydalanuvchi nomingizni yozing), **Public** qiling va yarating.
3. Repozitoriya sahifasida **Add file → Upload files** ni tanlang, sayt papkangizning ichidagi fayllarni (papkaning oʻzini emas) torting va **Commit changes** ni bosing.
4. **Settings → Pages** ni oching. **Build and deployment** boʻlimida manba **Deploy from a branch**, branch **main** va papka **/ (root)** ekanini tekshirib, saqlang.
5. Bir-ikki daqiqadan soʻng saytingiz `https://your-username.github.io/` manzilida ishlay boshlaydi.

## Saytni yangilash

Oʻzgargan fayllarni xuddi shu usulda yuklang yoki ularni bevosita GitHub’da tahrirlang. Har bir commit saytni bir-ikki daqiqa ichida qayta eʼlon qiladi. Oʻzgarishni koʻrmasangiz, sahifani **Ctrl + F5** (Windows) yoki **Cmd + Shift + R** (Mac) bilan yangilang.

> [!WARNING]
> Eʼlon qilingan sayt hammaga ochiq. Unga uy manzilingiz, telefon raqamingiz, pasport maʼlumotlaringiz yoki boshqa shaxsiy narsalarni joylamang.

## Natijani tekshirish

- Saytni kompyuterdan tashqari telefonda ham oching.
- Har bir havolani bosib koʻring va har bir rasm koʻrinishini tekshiring.
- Oldingi darsdagi klaviatura sinovini oʻtkazing.

## Oʻzingiz sinab koʻring

Oldingi loyihadagi profil sahifangizni eʼlon qiling. Havolani doʻstingizga yuboring va telefonida hammasi ishlayaptimi, deb soʻrang.

## Keng tarqalgan xatolar

- `index.html` eng yuqorida emas, ichki papkada turgani — bosh sahifa 404 xatosini koʻrsatadi.
- Fayl nomlaridan faqat katta-kichik harf bilan farq qiladigan havolalar.
- Nisbiy yoʻllar oʻrniga kompyuteringizdagi fayllarga (`C:\...`) ishora qiluvchi havolalar.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Veb-server** — brauzerlarga veb-sahifalarni yuboradigan kompyuter.
- **Statik sayt** — server tomonidagi kodsiz, tayyor fayllardan iborat sayt.
- **Repozitoriya** — GitHub’dagi tarixi bilan birga saqlanadigan loyiha papkasi.
- **Commit** — repozitoriyada saqlangan oʻzgarish.

## Programs that talk to people

So far your programs have printed fixed text. In this lesson you will write programs that **ask questions**, use the answers and reply — the basis of every interactive program.

## Output with print()

```python
print("Salom!")
print("Apples:", 5)
print("Done", end="")
```

`print()` can show several values separated by commas; it puts a space between them and starts a new line at the end. `end=""` stops it from moving to a new line.

## Input with input()

```python
name = input("What is your name? ")
print("Nice to meet you,", name)
```

`input()` shows the message, waits for the user to type something and press **Enter**, then returns what they typed.

> [!WARNING]
> `input()` always returns **text** (`str`), even if the user types a number. `"5" + "3"` gives `"53"`, not `8`.

## Turning text into numbers

```python
age = int(input("How old are you? "))
price = float(input("Price of one book: "))
print(age + 1)
print(price * 3)
```

- `int()` converts text such as `"17"` into a whole number.
- `float()` converts text such as `"2.5"` into a decimal number.

If the user types something that is not a number, such as `seventeen`, Python stops with a `ValueError`. You will learn to handle this gracefully in the lesson on errors.

## Friendly output with f-strings

An **f-string** has an `f` before the quotes and puts values inside curly braces:

```python
name = "Aziz"
lessons = 12
print(f"{name} has finished {lessons} lessons.")
print(f"Next year you will be {age + 1}.")
```

You can even format numbers: `f"{price:.2f}"` shows a number with exactly two decimal places.

## A worked example

```python
name = input("Name: ")
minutes = int(input("Minutes you studied today: "))
goal = 30
left = goal - minutes
print(f"Well done, {name}! {left} minutes left to reach your goal.")
```

If the user types `Malika` and `20`, the program prints: `Well done, Malika! 10 minutes left to reach your goal.`

## Try it

Write a program that asks for the price of a product and how many the user wants, then prints the total with two decimal places. Test it with `2.5` and `4` — the answer should be `10.00`.

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting that `input()` returns text and adding it to a number (`TypeError`).
- Forgetting the `f` before the quotes, so `{name}` is printed literally.
- Leaving out the space at the end of the input message, so the answer sticks to the question.

## Key terms

- **input()** — reads a line of text typed by the user.
- **print()** — shows values on the screen.
- **int() / float()** — convert text into a whole number or a decimal number.
- **f-string** — a string with values inserted in `{}`.

- Kiritish xabarining oxiridagi boʻsh joyni tashlab ketish — javob savolga yopishib qoladi.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **print()** — qiymatlarni ekranga chiqaradi.

## Questions with yes-or-no answers

Programs make decisions by asking questions whose answer is either **True** or **False**. In this lesson you will learn how to ask those questions in Python.

```python
print(10 > 3)
print(2 == 5)
```

The first line prints `True`, the second `False`. `True` and `False` are values of the type `bool` (boolean), named after the mathematician George Boole.

## Comparison operators

| Operator | Meaning | Example | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `==` | equal to | `5 == 5` | `True` |
| `!=` | not equal to | `5 != 3` | `True` |
| `<` | less than | `2 < 1` | `False` |
| `>` | greater than | `7 > 4` | `True` |
| `<=` | less than or equal to | `3 <= 3` | `True` |
| `>=` | greater than or equal to | `2 >= 5` | `False` |

> [!WARNING]
> `=` and `==` are different. `=` **stores** a value (`age = 17`); `==` **compares** two values (`age == 17`). Mixing them up is one of the most common beginner mistakes.

## Comparing text

Text can be compared too:

```python
print("apple" == "apple")
print("Apple" == "apple")
```

The first is `True`; the second is `False`, because comparisons are **case-sensitive**. To compare without caring about capitals, convert both sides first: `answer.lower() == "yes"`.

## Saving the result

A comparison is an expression like any other, so you can store its result:

```python
score = 82
passed = score >= 70
print(passed)
```

This prints `True`. Naming a boolean well — `passed`, `is_adult`, `has_ticket` — makes the code read like a sentence.

## Combining comparisons

Python lets you chain comparisons in a natural way:

```python
age = 15
print(13 <= age <= 19)
```

This asks “is `age` between 13 and 19?” and prints `True`.

## Try it

Ask the user for a number with `input()` and `int()`, then print whether it is greater than 100, whether it equals 0, and whether it is between 1 and 10.

## Common mistakes

- Writing `=` when you mean `==`.
- Comparing a number with text: `5 == "5"` is `False`, because one is an `int` and the other a `str`.
- Forgetting that `"Yes"` and `"yes"` are different strings.

## Key terms

- **Boolean (`bool`)** — a value that is either `True` or `False`.
- **Comparison operator** — a symbol such as `==` or `<` that compares two values.
- **Case-sensitive** — treating capital and small letters as different.
- **Expression** — a piece of code that produces a value.

## Javobi “ha” yoki “yoʻq” boʻlgan savollar

Dasturlar javobi **True** (rost) yoki **False** (yolgʻon) boʻlgan savollar berib qaror qabul qiladi. Bu darsda bunday savollarni Pythonda qanday berishni oʻrganasiz.

```python
print(10 > 3)
print(2 == 5)
```

Birinchi qator `True`, ikkinchisi `False` chiqaradi. `True` va `False` — matematik Jorj Bul nomi bilan atalgan `bool` (mantiqiy) turdagi qiymatlar.

## Taqqoslash operatorlari

| Operator | Maʼnosi | Misol | Natija |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `==` | teng | `5 == 5` | `True` |
| `!=` | teng emas | `5 != 3` | `True` |
| `<` | kichik | `2 < 1` | `False` |
| `>` | katta | `7 > 4` | `True` |
| `<=` | kichik yoki teng | `3 <= 3` | `True` |
| `>=` | katta yoki teng | `2 >= 5` | `False` |

> [!WARNING]
> `=` va `==` har xil. `=` qiymatni **saqlaydi** (`age = 17`); `==` ikki qiymatni **taqqoslaydi** (`age == 17`). Ularni chalkashtirish boshlovchilarning eng keng tarqalgan xatolaridan biri.

## Matnlarni taqqoslash

Matnlarni ham taqqoslash mumkin:

```python
print("olma" == "olma")
print("Olma" == "olma")
```

Birinchisi `True`; ikkinchisi `False`, chunki taqqoslash **katta-kichik harfga sezgir**. Bosh harflarga eʼtibor bermasdan taqqoslash uchun avval ikkala tomonni kichik harfga oʻtkazing: `answer.lower() == "ha"`.

## Natijani saqlash

Taqqoslash ham boshqa ifodalar kabi ifoda, shuning uchun uning natijasini saqlash mumkin:

```python
score = 82
passed = score >= 70
print(passed)
```

Bu `True` chiqaradi. Mantiqiy qiymatga yaxshi nom berish — `passed`, `is_adult`, `has_ticket` — kodni gap kabi oʻqiladigan qiladi.

## Taqqoslashlarni birlashtirish

Python taqqoslashlarni tabiiy tarzda zanjirga bogʻlash imkonini beradi:

```python
age = 15
print(13 <= age <= 19)
```

Bu “`age` 13 bilan 19 orasidami?” deb soʻraydi va `True` chiqaradi.

## Oʻzingiz sinab koʻring

Foydalanuvchidan `input()` va `int()` yordamida son soʻrang, soʻngra u 100 dan kattami, 0 ga tengmi va 1 bilan 10 orasidami — shularni chiqaring.

## Keng tarqalgan xatolar

- `==` nazarda tutilganda `=` yozish.
- Sonni matn bilan taqqoslash: `5 == "5"` natijasi `False`, chunki biri `int`, ikkinchisi `str`.
- `"Ha"` va `"ha"` har xil satrlar ekanini unutish.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Mantiqiy qiymat (`bool`)** — `True` yoki `False` boʻladigan qiymat.
- **Taqqoslash operatori** — ikki qiymatni taqqoslaydigan `==` yoki `<` kabi belgi.
- **Katta-kichik harfga sezgir** — bosh va kichik harflarni har xil deb hisoblash.
- **Ifoda** — qiymat hosil qiladigan kod boʻlagi.

contents.body_md:
## Choosing a path

Now that you can ask True-or-False questions, you can make your program **act** on the answer. In this lesson you will use `if`, `elif` and `else` to choose between different paths.

```python
temperature = int(input("Temperature today: "))

if temperature > 30:
    print("It is hot. Drink plenty of water.")
```

- The line with `if` ends with a **colon** `:`.
- The code that belongs to the `if` is **indented** by four spaces. Python uses indentation to know which lines are inside the decision.

## else: the other way

```python
if temperature > 30:
    print("It is hot.")
else:
    print("It is not too hot.")
```

Exactly one of the two blocks runs.

## elif: more than two choices

`elif` means “else, if”. Python checks the conditions from top to bottom and runs the **first** block whose condition is True:

```python
score = int(input("Your score: "))

if score >= 90:
    grade = "excellent"
elif score >= 70:
    grade = "good"
elif score >= 50:
    grade = "satisfactory"
else:
    grade = "needs more practice"

print(f"Result: {grade}")
```

A score of 75 gives “good” — Python stops checking as soon as `score >= 70` is True.

> [!TIP]
> Order matters. If you checked `score >= 50` first, a score of 95 would be reported as “satisfactory”. Put the strictest condition first.

## Combining conditions

- `and` — both conditions must be True.
- `or` — at least one condition must be True.
- `not` — reverses True and False.

```python
age = 16
has_permission = True

if age >= 18 or has_permission:
    print("You may join the trip.")
```

## Try it

Write a ticket price program: children under 7 travel free, people aged 7–17 pay 2 000 so‘m, adults pay 4 000 so‘m, and anyone with a student card pays half price. Test it with ages 5, 12 and 30.

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting the colon at the end of `if`, `elif` or `else`.
- Inconsistent indentation, which causes an `IndentationError`.
- Putting conditions in the wrong order, so a later branch is never reached.

## Key terms

- **if / elif / else** — keywords that choose which block of code runs.
- **Condition** — an expression that is True or False.
- **Indentation** — spaces at the start of a line that show which block it belongs to.
- **and / or / not** — operators that combine or reverse conditions.

## Yoʻlni tanlash

Endi True yoki False savollarini bera olasiz, demak, dasturingiz javobga qarab **harakat qila** oladi. Bu darsda turli yoʻllar orasidan tanlash uchun `if`, `elif` va `else` dan foydalanasiz.

```python

```

- `if` yozilgan qator **ikki nuqta** `:` bilan tugaydi.
- `if` ga tegishli kod toʻrt boʻsh joy bilan **chekinib** yoziladi. Python qaysi qatorlar shart ichida ekanini chekinish orqali biladi.

## else: boshqa yoʻl

```python

    print("Havo issiq.")
else:
    print("Havo unchalik issiq emas.")
```

Ikki blokdan aynan bittasi bajariladi.

## elif: ikkitadan koʻp tanlov

`elif` — “aks holda, agar” degani. Python shartlarni yuqoridan pastga qarab tekshiradi va sharti True boʻlgan **birinchi** blokni bajaradi:

## Shartlarni birlashtirish

- `and` — ikkala shart ham True boʻlishi kerak.
- `or` — kamida bitta shart True boʻlishi kerak.
- `not` — True va False ni teskarisiga aylantiradi.

- Chekinishlarning har xil boʻlishi — `IndentationError` xatosiga olib keladi.
- Shartlarni notoʻgʻri tartibda yozish — keyingi tarmoqqa hech qachon yetib borilmaydi.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **if / elif / else** — qaysi kod bloki bajarilishini tanlaydigan kalit soʻzlar.
- **Shart** — True yoki False boʻladigan ifoda.
- **Chekinish** — qator boshidagi, u qaysi blokka tegishli ekanini koʻrsatadigan boʻsh joylar.
- **and / or / not** — shartlarni birlashtiradigan yoki teskarisiga aylantiradigan operatorlar.

## Doing something again and again

Computers never get bored. A **loop** repeats a block of code, so you can do a task many times without writing it many times. In this lesson you will use the `while` loop, which repeats **as long as a condition is True**.

```python
count = 1
while count <= 5:
    print(count)
    count = count + 1
print("Finished")
```

This prints the numbers 1 to 5, then `Finished`. Step by step:

1. Python checks the condition `count <= 5`.
2. If it is True, it runs the indented block, then goes back to step 1.
3. When the condition is False, it continues after the loop.

## Updating the loop variable

The line `count = count + 1` is essential. Python also has a shorter way to write it: `count += 1`.

> [!WARNING]
> If nothing inside the loop ever makes the condition False, the loop runs **forever**. This is called an infinite loop. If it happens, press **Ctrl + C** in the terminal to stop the program.

## Loops that wait for the user

`while` is ideal when you do not know in advance how many times to repeat:

```python
answer = ""
while answer != "stop":
    answer = input("Type a word (or stop): ")
    print(f"You typed {len(answer)} letters.")
```

## Leaving a loop early with break

```python
secret = 7
while True:
    guess = int(input("Guess the number from 1 to 10: "))
    if guess == secret:
        print("Correct!")
        break
    print("Try again.")
```

`while True` would run forever, but `break` jumps out of the loop as soon as the guess is right.

## A worked example: a savings plan

```python
savings = 0
month = 0
while savings < 1000000:
    savings += 150000
    month += 1
print(f"You reach 1 000 000 so'm after {month} months.")
```

The loop adds 150 000 each month until the target is reached and then reports `7` months.

## Try it

Write a program that keeps asking the user for numbers and adds them up until they type `0`, then prints the total.

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting to update the variable in the condition, which creates an infinite loop.
- Using `=` instead of `==` or `!=` in the condition.
- Putting the update outside the indented block, so it runs only after the loop.

## Key terms

- **Loop** — code that repeats.
- **while loop** — repeats while a condition is True.
- **Infinite loop** — a loop whose condition never becomes False.
- **break** — leaves a loop immediately.

## Bir ishni qayta-qayta bajarish

Kompyuterlar hech qachon zerikmaydi. **Sikl** kod blokini takrorlaydi, shuning uchun bir vazifani koʻp marta yozmasdan, koʻp marta bajarishingiz mumkin. Bu darsda **shart True boʻlib turgan ekan** takrorlanadigan `while` siklidan foydalanasiz.

```python
count = 1
while count <= 5:
    print(count)
    count = count + 1
print("Tugadi")
```

Bu 1 dan 5 gacha sonlarni, soʻngra `Tugadi` ni chiqaradi. Qadamma-qadam:

1. Python `count <= 5` shartini tekshiradi.
2. Agar u True boʻlsa, chekinib yozilgan blokni bajaradi va 1-qadamga qaytadi.
3. Shart False boʻlganda sikldan keyingi kodga oʻtadi.

## Sikl oʻzgaruvchisini yangilash

`count = count + 1` qatori juda muhim. Pythonda uni qisqaroq yozish usuli ham bor: `count += 1`.

> [!WARNING]
> Agar sikl ichidagi hech narsa shartni False ga aylantirmasa, sikl **abadiy** davom etadi. Bu cheksiz sikl deb ataladi. Shunday boʻlsa, dasturni toʻxtatish uchun terminalda **Ctrl + C** ni bosing.

## Foydalanuvchini kutadigan sikllar

`while` necha marta takrorlash kerakligini oldindan bilmaganingizda juda qulay:

```python
answer = ""
while answer != "stop":
    answer = input("Soʻz yozing (yoki stop): ")
    print(f"Siz {len(answer)} ta harf yozdingiz.")
```

## break bilan sikldan erta chiqish

```python
secret = 7
while True:
    guess = int(input("1 dan 10 gacha sonni toping: "))
    if guess == secret:
        print("Toʻgʻri!")
        break
    print("Yana urinib koʻring.")
```

`while True` abadiy davom etardi, ammo taxmin toʻgʻri boʻlishi bilanoq `break` sikldan chiqib ketadi.

## Ishlangan misol: jamgʻarma rejasi

```python
savings = 0
month = 0
while savings < 1000000:
    savings += 150000
    month += 1
print(f"{month} oydan keyin 1 000 000 so'm yigʻasiz.")
```

Sikl maqsadga yetguncha har oy 150 000 qoʻshadi va natijada `7` oyni koʻrsatadi.

## Oʻzingiz sinab koʻring

Foydalanuvchidan `0` yozguncha sonlarni soʻrab, ularni qoʻshib boradigan, soʻngra yigʻindini chiqaradigan dastur yozing.

## Keng tarqalgan xatolar

- Shartdagi oʻzgaruvchini yangilashni unutish — cheksiz sikl paydo boʻladi.
- Shartda `==` yoki `!=` oʻrniga `=` ishlatish.
- Yangilash qatorini chekinib yozilgan blokdan tashqariga qoʻyish — u faqat sikldan keyin bajariladi.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Sikl** — takrorlanadigan kod.
- **while sikli** — shart True boʻlib turgan ekan takrorlanadi.
- **Cheksiz sikl** — sharti hech qachon False boʻlmaydigan sikl.
- **break** — sikldan darhol chiqadi.

## Going through a sequence

A `for` loop takes the items of a sequence **one by one**. It is the loop you will use most often. In this lesson you will repeat code a fixed number of times and walk through text and lists.

```python
for letter in "Salom":
    print(letter)
```

This prints `S`, `a`, `l`, `o`, `m` on separate lines. Each time round the loop, the variable `letter` holds the next character.

## Counting with range()

`range()` produces a sequence of numbers:

| Code | Numbers produced |
| --- | --- |
| `range(5)` | 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| `range(1, 6)` | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 |
| `range(0, 10, 2)` | 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 |
| `range(5, 0, -1)` | 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 |

> [!NOTE]
> `range(5)` stops **before** 5. The end number is never included — a detail that surprises almost everyone at first.

```python
for i in range(1, 4):
    print(f"Lesson {i}")
```

## Building up a result

A very common pattern is to start with an empty or zero value and build it up inside the loop:

```python
total = 0
for number in range(1, 11):
    total += number
print(total)
```

This adds 1 to 10 and prints `55`.

## Skipping with continue

`continue` skips the rest of the current round and moves on to the next item:

```python
for n in range(1, 11):
    if n % 2 == 0:
        continue
    print(n)
```

`%` gives the remainder of a division, so `n % 2 == 0` is True for even numbers. The program prints only the odd numbers.

## while or for?

- Use **for** when you know how many times to repeat, or you are going through every item.
- Use **while** when you repeat until something happens, such as the user typing “stop”.

## Try it

Print a multiplication table for a number the user chooses, from 1 to 10, in the form `7 x 3 = 21`.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting `range(10)` to include 10.
- Changing the loop variable inside a `for` loop and expecting it to affect the next round.
- Forgetting to indent the body of the loop.

## Key terms

- **for loop** — repeats once for each item of a sequence.
- **range()** — produces a sequence of whole numbers.
- **continue** — skips to the next round of the loop.
- **Remainder (`%`)** — what is left over after division.

## Many values in one place

Imagine storing the marks of 30 students in 30 separate variables. A **list** keeps them all in one variable, in order. In this lesson you will create, read, change and loop over lists.

```python
cities = ["Tashkent", "Samarkand", "Bukhara"]
marks = [5, 4, 5, 3]
empty = []
```

A list is written with square brackets, and its items are separated by commas. Items can be of any type.

## Reading items by index

Each item has a position number called an **index**. Counting starts at **0**:

```python
print(cities[0])
print(cities[2])
print(cities[-1])
```

This prints `Tashkent`, `Bukhara` and `Bukhara` — a negative index counts from the end.

> [!WARNING]
> Asking for an index that does not exist, such as `cities[3]` in a three-item list, stops the program with an `IndexError`.

## Changing a list

| Code | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cities.append("Khiva")` | Adds an item to the end |
| `cities.insert(0, "Nukus")` | Inserts an item at position 0 |
| `cities.remove("Bukhara")` | Removes the first matching item |
| `cities[1] = "Andijan"` | Replaces the item at position 1 |
| `cities.sort()` | Sorts the list in place |

## Useful questions about a list

```python
marks = [5, 4, 5, 3]
print(len(marks))
print(sum(marks) / len(marks))
print(4 in marks)
print(max(marks), min(marks))
```

`len()` gives the number of items, `sum()` adds them, `in` checks whether an item is present, and `max()` and `min()` find the largest and smallest.

## Looping over a list

```python
for city in cities:
    print(f"I would like to visit {city}.")
```

## Taking part of a list

A **slice** takes several items at once: `marks[1:3]` gives the items at positions 1 and 2, `[4, 5]`. As with `range()`, the end position is not included.

## Try it

Make an empty list called `shopping`. Use a `while` loop to ask the user for items until they type `done`, adding each one with `append()`. Then print how many items there are and each item on its own line.

## Common mistakes

- Starting to count at 1 instead of 0.
- Using an index that is too large.
- Writing `cities.append = "Khiva"` instead of calling `cities.append("Khiva")`.

## Key terms

- **List** — an ordered collection of values.
- **Index** — the position of an item, starting at 0.
- **Method** — a function that belongs to a value, such as `append()`.
- **Slice** — part of a list, such as `marks[1:3]`.

## Looking things up by name

A list finds items by position. A **dictionary** finds values by a **key** — like a real dictionary, where you look up a word to find its meaning. In this lesson you will store and look up information with dictionaries.

```python
student = {
    "name": "Malika",
    "age": 16,
    "city": "Namangan",
}
```

A dictionary uses curly braces. Each entry is a **key–value pair** written `key: value`.

## Reading values

```python
print(student["name"])
print(student.get("phone", "not given"))
```

The first line prints `Malika`. Square brackets stop the program with a `KeyError` if the key is missing, so `get()` is safer: it returns the second value (`"not given"`) when the key does not exist.

## Adding and changing entries

```python
student["phone"] = "+998 90 123 45 67"
student["age"] = 17
del student["city"]
```

Assigning to a new key adds it; assigning to an existing key replaces its value; `del` removes an entry.

## Looping over a dictionary

```python
prices = {"bread": 4000, "milk": 12000, "tea": 25000}

for item, price in prices.items():
    print(f"{item}: {price} so'm")
```

`items()` gives each key together with its value.

## Counting with a dictionary

Dictionaries are perfect for counting:

```python
text = "olma anor olma uzum olma"
counts = {}
for word in text.split():
    counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1
print(counts)
```

This prints `{'olma': 3, 'anor': 1, 'uzum': 1}`. `split()` breaks the text into words.

> [!TIP]
> Use a list when order matters and items are similar (a queue of names). Use a dictionary when you look things up by a label (a price for each product).

## Try it

Create a dictionary of five English words and their Uzbek translations. Ask the user for an English word and print the translation, or “Not in the dictionary yet” if it is missing.

## Common mistakes

- Using square brackets for a key that may not exist, instead of `get()`.
- Forgetting the quotes around text keys: `student[name]` instead of `student["name"]`.
- Expecting a dictionary to be sorted by value.

## Key terms

- **Dictionary (`dict`)** — a collection of key–value pairs.
- **Key** — the label used to look up a value.
- **get()** — reads a value, with a default if the key is missing.
- **items()** — gives keys and values together in a loop.

## Keeping data after the program ends

Variables disappear when a program stops. To keep data — a to-do list, scores, expenses — you save it in a **file**. In this lesson you will write and read text files, and handle errors so your program does not crash.

## Writing a file

```python
with open("notes.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("Oʻzbekcha matn ham toʻgʻri saqlanadi.\n")
    f.write("Second line\n")
```

- `open()` opens a file; `"w"` means **write** (it creates the file, or replaces it if it exists).
- `with` closes the file automatically when the block ends, even if something goes wrong.
- `encoding="utf-8"` makes sure every alphabet, including oʻ, gʻ and Cyrillic, is saved correctly.
- `\n` starts a new line.

## Reading a file

```python
with open("notes.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.strip())
```

The default mode is `"r"` (read). Looping over the file gives one line at a time; `strip()` removes the line break at the end.

| Mode | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"r"` | Read (the default); the file must exist |
| `"w"` | Write; replaces everything in the file |
| `"a"` | Append; adds to the end of the file |

## When things go wrong

Errors are normal: the user types letters where a number is expected, or a file does not exist. Python reports these as **exceptions**. Without handling, the program stops and prints a **traceback** — read it from the bottom: the last line names the error, the lines above show where it happened.

## Handling errors with try and except

```python
try:
    age = int(input("Your age: "))
    print(f"Next year you will be {age + 1}.")
except ValueError:
    print("Please type your age in digits, for example 17.")
```

If the code inside `try` raises a `ValueError`, Python jumps to the `except` block instead of crashing.

```python
try:
    with open("scores.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        print(f.read())
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("No scores saved yet.")
```

> [!TIP]
> Catch only the errors you expect and know how to handle, such as `ValueError` or `FileNotFoundError`. Catching every error hides real bugs.

## Try it

Write a program that asks for a short note, appends it to `diary.txt` with mode `"a"`, then prints all the notes saved so far. Make it print a friendly message instead of crashing if the file does not exist yet.

## Common mistakes

- Using `"w"` when you meant `"a"` and wiping the file.
- Forgetting `encoding="utf-8"`, so Uzbek or Russian letters are garbled on some computers.
- Wrapping a whole program in `try` / `except` and hiding mistakes.

## Key terms

- **File mode** — how a file is opened: read, write or append.
- **Encoding (UTF-8)** — how text is turned into bytes; UTF-8 supports every alphabet.
- **Exception** — an error that happens while a program runs.
- **Traceback** — Python's report showing where an error happened.

## Dastur tugagandan keyin ham maʼlumotni saqlash

Dastur toʻxtaganda oʻzgaruvchilar yoʻqoladi. Maʼlumotlarni — vazifalar roʻyxati, natijalar, xarajatlarni — saqlab qolish uchun ularni **fayl**ga yozasiz. Bu darsda matnli fayllarni yozasiz va oʻqiysiz hamda dasturingiz ishdan chiqmasligi uchun xatolarni boshqarasiz.

## Faylga yozish

```python
with open("notes.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("Oʻzbekcha matn ham toʻgʻri saqlanadi.\n")
    f.write("Ikkinchi qator\n")
```

- `open()` faylni ochadi; `"w"` — **yozish** rejimi (faylni yaratadi yoki, agar u mavjud boʻlsa, almashtiradi).
- `with` blok tugaganda, hatto biror narsa notoʻgʻri ketsa ham, faylni avtomatik yopadi.
- `encoding="utf-8"` barcha alifbolar, jumladan, oʻ, gʻ va kirill harflari toʻgʻri saqlanishini taʼminlaydi.
- `\n` yangi qatorni boshlaydi.

## Fayldan oʻqish

```python
with open("notes.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.strip())
```

Standart rejim — `"r"` (oʻqish). Fayl boʻylab sikl har safar bitta qatorni beradi; `strip()` qator oxiridagi yangi qator belgisini olib tashlaydi.

| Rejim | Maʼnosi |
| --- | --- |
| `"r"` | Oʻqish (standart); fayl mavjud boʻlishi shart |
| `"w"` | Yozish; fayldagi hamma narsani almashtiradi |
| `"a"` | Qoʻshish; fayl oxiriga yozadi |

## Biror narsa notoʻgʻri ketganda

Xatolar — odatiy hol: foydalanuvchi son kutilgan joyga harf yozadi yoki fayl mavjud boʻlmaydi. Python bularni **istisno** (*exception*) sifatida xabar qiladi. Ular boshqarilmasa, dastur toʻxtaydi va **traceback** chiqaradi — uni pastdan yuqoriga qarab oʻqing: oxirgi qator xato nomini, yuqoridagi qatorlar esa u qayerda sodir boʻlganini koʻrsatadi.

## try va except bilan xatolarni boshqarish

```python
try:
    age = int(input("Yoshingiz: "))
    print(f"Kelasi yili {age + 1} yoshga toʻlasiz.")
except ValueError:
    print("Iltimos, yoshingizni raqamlar bilan yozing, masalan, 17.")
```

Agar `try` ichidagi kod `ValueError` bersa, Python ishdan chiqish oʻrniga `except` blokiga oʻtadi.

```python
try:
    with open("scores.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        print(f.read())
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Hali hech qanday natija saqlanmagan.")
```

> [!TIP]
> Faqat kutgan va qanday boshqarishni biladigan xatolaringizni, masalan, `ValueError` yoki `FileNotFoundError` ni ushlang. Har qanday xatoni ushlash haqiqiy xatolarni yashiradi.

## Oʻzingiz sinab koʻring

Qisqa qayd soʻrab, uni `"a"` rejimida `diary.txt` fayliga qoʻshadigan, soʻngra shu paytgacha saqlangan barcha qaydlarni chiqaradigan dastur yozing. Fayl hali mavjud boʻlmasa, dastur ishdan chiqish oʻrniga tushunarli xabar chiqarsin.

## Keng tarqalgan xatolar

- `"a"` nazarda tutilganda `"w"` dan foydalanib, faylni tozalab yuborish.
- `encoding="utf-8"` ni unutish — natijada baʼzi kompyuterlarda oʻzbek yoki rus harflari buzilib ketadi.
- Butun dasturni `try` / `except` ichiga olib, xatolarni yashirish.

## Asosiy atamalar

- **Fayl rejimi** — fayl qanday ochilishi: oʻqish, yozish yoki qoʻshish.
- **Kodlash (UTF-8)** — matnni baytlarga aylantirish usuli; UTF-8 barcha alifbolarni qoʻllab-quvvatlaydi.
- **Istisno** (*exception*) — dastur ishlayotgan paytda yuz beradigan xato.
- **Traceback** — xato qayerda sodir boʻlganini koʻrsatadigan Python hisoboti.

## Your first complete program

Build a **quiz game** that asks the player several questions, checks the answers and reports a score. It uses almost everything you have learned: variables, input, conditions, loops, lists, dictionaries and functions.

### Requirements

1. Store at least **five questions** in a list of dictionaries, each with a question and its answer, for example `{"question": "Capital of Uzbekistan?", "answer": "tashkent"}`.
2. Ask the questions one by one with a loop.
3. Compare answers without caring about capitals or spaces (use `lower()` and `strip()`).
4. Keep a score and tell the player after each question whether they were right — and the right answer if not.
5. Put the checking code in a function, for example `check_answer(given, correct)`.
6. At the end, print the score and a message that depends on it (for example, “Excellent!” for full marks).

### Ideas for extra challenge

- Let the player play again without restarting the program.
- Save the best score to a file and show it at the start.

### How to submit

Paste your code into the text box or upload your `.py` file, and add the output of one complete game.

> [!NOTE]
> A reviewer checks your program against the rubric and leaves feedback. You can improve it and resubmit.

## Birinchi toʻliq dasturingiz

Oʻyinchiga bir nechta savol beradigan, javoblarni tekshiradigan va natijani maʼlum qiladigan **viktorina oʻyini**ni yarating. U siz oʻrgangan deyarli hamma narsadan foydalanadi: oʻzgaruvchilar, kiritish, shartlar, sikllar, roʻyxatlar, lugʻatlar va funksiyalar.

### Talablar

1. Kamida **beshta savolni** lugʻatlar roʻyxatida saqlang; har birida savol va uning javobi boʻlsin, masalan, `{"question": "Oʻzbekiston poytaxti?", "answer": "toshkent"}`.
2. Savollarni sikl yordamida birma-bir bering.
3. Javoblarni bosh harf va boʻsh joylarga eʼtibor bermasdan taqqoslang (`lower()` va `strip()` dan foydalaning).
4. Ballni hisoblab boring va har bir savoldan keyin oʻyinchiga toʻgʻri javob berganini — agar notoʻgʻri boʻlsa, toʻgʻri javobni — ayting.
5. Tekshirish kodini funksiyaga joylang, masalan, `check_answer(given, correct)`.
6. Oxirida ballni va unga bogʻliq xabarni chiqaring (masalan, toʻliq ball uchun “Aʼlo!”).

### Qoʻshimcha murakkablik uchun gʻoyalar

- Oʻyinchiga dasturni qayta ishga tushirmasdan yana oʻynash imkonini bering.
- Eng yaxshi natijani faylga saqlang va uni boshida koʻrsating.

### Qanday topshiriladi

Kodingizni matn maydoniga joylang yoki `.py` faylingizni yuklang va bitta toʻliq oʻyin natijasini ham qoʻshing.

> [!NOTE]
> Tekshiruvchi dasturingizni baholash mezonlari asosida koʻrib chiqadi va fikr-mulohaza qoldiradi. Uni yaxshilab, qayta topshirishingiz mumkin.

## A tool you can actually use

Build a **personal budget tracker** that runs in the terminal, remembers expenses between runs and shows totals by category.

### Requirements

1. A menu that repeats until the user chooses to quit, for example: `1) Add expense  2) Show all  3) Totals by category  4) Quit`.
2. **Add expense** asks for an amount and a category (such as food, transport or books). Invalid amounts are handled with `try` / `except` instead of crashing.
3. Expenses are saved to a text file (for example, one line per expense: `25000,food`) and loaded again when the program starts.
4. **Show all** lists every expense.
5. **Totals by category** uses a dictionary to add up the amounts per category and prints the grand total.
6. Use at least three functions, such as `load_expenses()`, `save_expense()` and `totals_by_category()`.

### Ideas for extra challenge

- Show the largest expense and its category.
- Print amounts with spaces between thousands, such as `1 250 000 so'm`.

### How to submit

Paste your code or upload your `.py` file, and include a short example session that shows adding an expense, closing the program, opening it again and seeing the expense still there.

> [!NOTE]
> A reviewer checks your program against the rubric and leaves feedback. You can improve it and resubmit.

## Haqiqatan ishlatsa boʻladigan vosita

Terminalda ishlaydigan, xarajatlarni ishga tushirishlar orasida eslab qoladigan va toifalar boʻyicha jami summalarni koʻrsatadigan **shaxsiy byudjet hisobchisi**ni yarating.

### Talablar

1. Foydalanuvchi chiqishni tanlaguncha takrorlanadigan menyu, masalan: `1) Xarajat qoʻshish  2) Hammasini koʻrsatish  3) Toifalar boʻyicha jami  4) Chiqish`.
2. **Xarajat qoʻshish** summa va toifani (masalan, oziq-ovqat, transport yoki kitoblar) soʻraydi. Notoʻgʻri summalar dastur ishdan chiqishi oʻrniga `try` / `except` bilan boshqariladi.
3. Xarajatlar matnli faylga saqlanadi (masalan, har bir xarajat uchun bitta qator: `25000,food`) va dastur ishga tushganda qayta yuklanadi.
4. **Hammasini koʻrsatish** barcha xarajatlarni roʻyxat qilib chiqaradi.
5. **Toifalar boʻyicha jami** har bir toifa summalarini lugʻat yordamida qoʻshadi va umumiy summani chiqaradi.
6. Kamida uchta funksiyadan foydalaning, masalan, `load_expenses()`, `save_expense()` va `totals_by_category()`.

### Qoʻshimcha murakkablik uchun gʻoyalar
